We shall now present what clarifies what we have said. The hadiths concerning punishment in the grave and the questioning by Munkar and Nakīr are numerous and mass-transmitted from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace). Among them is the report in the two Sahīh collections from Ibn ‘Abbās (may Allah be pleased with them both):

“The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) passed by two graves and said, ‘Both of them are being punished, yet they are not being punished for anything great. One of them used to go about spreading malicious gossip, while the other did not protect himself from his urine.’ Then he asked for a fresh palm frond, split it in two, and planted one half in each grave. They asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, why have you done this?’ He replied, ‘Perhaps their punishment will be lightened so long as these two do not dry out.’”

In Sahīh Muslim, Zayd ibn Thābit said:

“While the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) was riding a mule in a garden belonging to Banū al-Najjār, with us accompanying him, it suddenly swerved and nearly threw him off. There were six, five, or four graves there. He asked, ‘Who knows about these graves?’ A man replied, ‘I do.’ He asked, ‘When did these people die?’ The man replied, ‘They died in a state of polytheism.’ He said, ‘This community is indeed put to trial in its graves. Were it not that you might cease burying one another, I would ask Allah to let you hear some of the punishment of the grave that I hear.’

“Then he turned to face us and said, ‘Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave.’ They said, ‘We seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the grave.’

“He said, ‘Seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire.’ They said, ‘We seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Fire.’

“He said, ‘Seek refuge in Allah from trials, both manifest and hidden.’ They said, ‘We seek refuge in Allah from trials, both manifest and hidden.’

“He said, ‘Seek refuge in Allah from the trial of the Dajjāl.’ They said, ‘We seek refuge in Allah from the trial of the Dajjāl.’”

“When any of you has finished the final tashahhud (testimony of faith), let him say, ‘I seek refuge in Allah from four things: the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the trial of the false messiah, the Dajjāl.’”

In Sahīh Muslim and elsewhere, Ibn ‘Abbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) reports that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) used to teach them this supplication just as he would teach them a surah of the Quran:

“O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell; I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave; I seek refuge in You from the trial of the false messiah, the Dajjāl; and I seek refuge in You from the trials of life and death.”

In Sahīh al-Bukhārī and Sahīh Muslim, Abū Ayyūb al-Ansārī said:

“The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) went out after the sun had set and said, ‘Some Jews are being punished in their graves.’”

In the two Sahīh collections, ‘Ā’ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said:

“An elderly Jewish woman from Medina came to me and said, ‘The people in the graves are being punished in their graves.’ I rejected what she said and could not bring myself to believe her. She left, and the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) came to me. I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, an elderly woman from Medina came to me and claimed that the people in the graves are being punished in their graves.’

“He replied, ‘She spoke the truth. They are indeed suffering a punishment that all animals can hear.’ After that, I never saw him pray without seeking refuge from the punishment of the grave.”

translated_text:
the grave.’ I said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, is there punishment in the grave?’ He replied, ‘They are indeed being punished in their graves with a punishment that animals can hear.’”

Some have said: This is why people take their animals, when they suffer from colic, to the graves of Jews, Christians and hypocrites, such as the Ismā‘īlīs, the Nusayrīs and the other Qarmatians, including Banū ‘Ubayd and others in Egypt, Syria and elsewhere. Horse owners deliberately visit their graves for this purpose, just as they visit the graves of Jews and Christians. The ignorant suppose that they are descendants of Fātimah and among Allah’s righteous allies, whereas this is merely an instance of what has just been described. For it has been said that when horses hear the punishment of the grave, they develop a heat that dispels their colic.

There are many hadiths on this, more than the scope of this question permits us to discuss. There are also many hadiths concerning this matter, including the report in Sahīh al-Bukhārī, Sahīh Muslim and the Sunan collections from al-Barā’ ibn ‘Āzib (may Allah be pleased with him), who reported that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said:

“When a Muslim is questioned in his grave, he testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. This is what Allah Most High means by His words: ‘Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter.’”

Another wording states:

“This was revealed concerning the punishment of the grave. He is asked, ‘Who is your Lord?’ He replies, ‘My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad.’ This is what Allah Most High means by His words: ‘Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And Allah sends astray the wrongdoers. And Allah does what He wills.’”

The compilers of the Sunan and Musnad collections have narrated this hadith at length, as in Sunan Abī Dāwūd

The hadith thus explicitly states that the soul is restored to the body and that his ribs interlock. This clearly indicates that the punishment afflicts both the soul and the body together.

A report similar to the hadith of al-Barā’, concerning the taking of the soul, the questioning, the bliss and the punishment, has also been narrated by Abū Hurayrah. He replies, ‘Muhammad. We bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, who brought the truth from Allah.’

He is told, ‘Upon this belief you lived, and upon it you will be resurrected, if Allah wills.’ Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he is told, ‘This is your dwelling and what Allah has prepared for you there.’ His joy and happiness increase. Then his grave is widened for him by seventy cubits and illuminated. His body is returned to that from which it originated, and his soul becomes the spirit of a bird feeding among the trees of Paradise. He said: This is what Allah Most High says:

‘Allah keeps those who believe firm with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And Allah leaves the wrongdoers astray, and Allah does what He wills.’”

Regarding disbelief, he mentioned the opposite, saying: “His grave is constricted around him until his ribs interlock. This is the life of hardship of which Allah Most High says:

‘He will have a life of hardship, and We will raise him blind on the Day of Resurrection.’”

This hadith is shorter. The previously cited hadith of al-Barā’ is the longest in the Sunan collections; their compilers abridged it to present what it contains concerning the punishment of the grave. It appears in full in al-Musnad and elsewhere.

It is a sound, established hadith, in which the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) says:

“When the believing servant is approaching the Hereafter and departing from this world, angels with radiant faces, as though their faces were the sun, descend to him.  مِنْهَا: أَنَّ الرُّوحَ تَبْقَى بَعْدَ مُفَارَقَةِ الْبَدَنِ؛ خِلَافًا لِضُلَّالِ الْمُتَكَلِّمِينَ؛ وَأَنَّهَا تَصْعَدُ وَتَنْزِلُ خِلَافًا لِضُلَّالِ الْفَلَاسِفَةِ؛ وَأَنَّهَا تُعَادُ إلَى الْبَدَنِ وَأَنَّ الْمَيِّتَ يُسْأَلُ فَيُنَعَّمُ أَوْ يُعَذَّبُ كَمَا سَأَلَ عَنْهُ أَهْلُ السُّؤَالِ وَفِيهِ أَنَّ عَمَلَهُ الصَّالِحَ أَوْ السَّيِّئَ يَأْتِيهِ فِي صُورَةٍ حَسَنَةٍ أَوْ قَبِيحَةٍ. وَفِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ عَنْ قتادة عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ
translated_text:
and whenever they pass a company of angels, they ask, ‘What is this wicked soul?’ They reply, ‘So-and-so, son of so-and-so,’ using the ugliest names by which he was known in this world. They bring it to the lowest heaven and ask for it to be opened for it, but it is not opened. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited:

‘The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. Thus do We recompense the criminals.’

Then Allah Most High says, ‘Enter his record in Sijjīn—in the lowest earth.’ He said: His soul is then flung down. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited:

‘Or the wind sweeps him away to a far-off place.’

He said: His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and sit him up. They ask him, ‘Who is your Lord?’ He replies, ‘Ah, ah! I do not know.’”

He related the hadith as above until he said: “A man with an ugly face and a foul stench comes to him and says, ‘Receive tidings of what will distress you! This is your deed, which you were promised.’ He asks, ‘Who are you? Yours is a face that brings no good.’ He replies, ‘I am your evil deeds.’ Then he says three times, ‘My Lord, do not bring on the Hour!’”

This hadith contains various kinds of knowledge. Among them is that the soul continues to exist after leaving the body, contrary to the misguided speculative theologians; that it ascends and descends, contrary to the misguided philosophers; that it is returned to the body; and that the deceased is questioned and then granted bliss or subjected to punishment, as those who submitted the question had asked about. It also establishes that his righteous or evil deeds come to him in a beautiful or ugly form.

“I do not know. I used to hear people saying something, so I said it.” The two angels say, “We knew that you would say that.” Then the earth is told, “Close in upon him.” It closes in upon him until his ribs interlock, and he continues to be tormented until Allah raises him from that resting place.’”

This hadith mentions his ribs interlocking, along with other details that make clear that the body itself is tormented.

Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a person is dying, the angels come to him with a white silk cloth. They say, ‘Come out with a fragrance like the finest musk.’ They pass the soul from one to another until they bring it to the gate of heaven. Those there say, ‘How lovely this fragrance is! When did it come to you from the earth?’ They then bring it to the souls of the believers, who rejoice at its arrival more than any of you rejoices when someone absent returns to him. They ask him, ‘What has so-and-so done?’ Then they say, ‘Leave him, for he is in the distress of worldly life.’ When he says, ‘He has come to you,’ they say, ‘He has gone to his mother, the Abyss.’

“When a disbeliever is dying, the angels of punishment come to him with a cloth of wool or hair. They say, ‘Come out, under Allah’s wrath, to Allah’s punishment.’ The soul comes out smelling like the foulest carcass, and they bring it to the souls of the disbelievers.”

This was narrated by al-Nasā’ī and al-Bazzār. Muslim narrated an abridged version from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. At the mention of the disbeliever and the foul smell of his soul, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, drew a wrap he was wearing over his nose, like this. A raytah is a thin, soft cloth, like a sheet.

translated_text:

What has such-and-such a woman done?’ As for the disbeliever, when his soul is taken, it is brought to the earth. The keepers of the earth say, ‘We have never encountered a stench fouler than this,’ and it is taken down to the lowest earth.”

These hadiths and others like them describe the soul and body sharing in the bliss and torment of the grave. As for what the soul experiences on its own, some of that has already been discussed.

Kaʿb ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The believer’s soul is a bird that feeds among the trees of Paradise until Allah returns it to its body on the day He resurrects him.”

This was narrated by al-Nasā’ī, and also by both Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī. The word “yaʿlaqu,” read with a u vowel, means “to eat.” This has also been reported in other hadiths. These texts tell us that the soul enjoys bliss together with the body in the grave—if Allah wills—whereas it enjoys bliss in Paradise on its own. Both are true.

Ibn Abī al-Dunyā narrated in his book Dhikr al-Mawt (The Remembrance of Death) that Mālik ibn Anas said:

“It has reached me that the soul is released to go wherever it wishes.”

This agrees with the report that “the soul may be in the open spaces around the graves.” As Mujāhid said, “Souls remain at the graves for seven days from the day the deceased is buried, without departing; and the soul may be returned to the body at times other than the questioning.” This is illustrated by the hadith that Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr authenticated, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“No man passes by the grave of a man he knew in this world and greets him with peace without Allah restoring the deceased’s soul to him so that he may return the greeting.”

translated_text:
In the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and elsewhere, Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafī reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The best of your days is Friday, so send abundant blessings upon me on Friday and the night preceding it, for your blessings are presented to me.”

They asked, “O Messenger of Allah, how will our blessings be presented to you when you have decayed?”

He replied, “Allah has forbidden the earth to consume the bodies of the prophets.”

There are more hadiths and reports on this subject than time presently permits us to examine exhaustively. They make clear that bodies in their graves experience bliss and torment—if Allah wills it—in whatever manner He wills, and that souls continue to exist after leaving the body, experiencing bliss and torment. For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded that the dead be greeted with peace, as established in the Sahīh and Sunan collections:

“He would teach his Companions, when they visited the graves, to say: ‘Peace be upon you, believing inhabitants of these dwellings. We shall, if Allah wills, join you. May Allah have mercy on those among us and you who have gone before and those who come after. We ask Allah for well-being for ourselves and for you. O Allah, do not deprive us of the reward associated with them, do not subject us to trials after them, and forgive us and them.’”

This has been disclosed to many people, who have heard the voices of those being tormented in their graves and seen with their own eyes those undergoing torment there, as recounted in numerous well-known reports. However, this need not affect the body continuously at every moment; rather, it may occur at some times and not at others.

translated_text:
In the two Sahīh collections, Anas ibn Mālik, may Allah be pleased with him, reported:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, left those slain at Badr for three days. Then he came to them, stood over them, and said: ‘O Abū Jahl ibn Hishām! O Umayyah ibn Khalaf! O ‘Utbah ibn Rabī‘ah! O Shaybah ibn Rabī‘ah! Have you not found what your Lord promised you to be true? I have indeed found what my Lord promised me to be true.’

‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, heard the Prophet’s words and asked: ‘O Messenger of Allah, how can they hear when their bodies have putrefied?’

He replied: ‘By Him in Whose hand is my soul, you hear what I say no better than they do, but they cannot answer.’ Then he ordered that they be dragged away and thrown into the well of Badr.”

Both compilers also recorded in their Sahīh collections the report of Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood beside the well of Badr and said: ‘Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?’ He also said: ‘They can indeed now hear what I am saying.’

This was mentioned to ‘Ā’ishah, who said: ‘Ibn ‘Umar was mistaken. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said: “They now know that what I told them is the truth.”’ Then she recited the words of the Most High, ‘You cannot make the dead hear,’ continuing to the end of the verse.”

Scholars of hadith and the Sunnah agree that the reports narrated by Anas and Ibn ‘Umar are authentic, even though neither attended Badr. Anas narrated this from Abū Talhah, who did attend Badr.

Thus, Abū Hātim recorded in his Sahīh, from Anas, from Abū Talhah, may Allah be pleased with him:

“On the day of Badr, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered that twenty-four of the leading men of Quraysh be thrown into one of the stone-lined wells of Badr. Whenever he prevailed over a people, he liked to remain on their grounds for three nights:

so when the third day came, he called for his mount, secured its saddle and set it in motion, then walked on, followed by his Companions. They said: ‘We think he is only going to attend to some need.’ He continued until he stood at the edge of the well, then began calling them by their names and their fathers’ names: ‘O so-and-so, son of so-and-so! Would you be glad if you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?’

‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, you are only speaking to bodies with no souls in them.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, replied: ‘By Him in Whose hand is my soul, you hear what I say no better than they do.’”

Qatādah said: “Allah brought them to life so that they heard, to rebuke and humiliate them, to punish them and cause them anguish and remorse.”

‘Ā’ishah interpreted the matter she mentioned, just as she interpreted other similar matters. An authentic statement from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, takes precedence over the interpretation of any of his Companions or anyone else. Nothing in the Quran negates this, for His words,

“You cannot make the dead hear,”

refer only to the ordinary hearing that benefits the hearer. This is a comparison drawn for the disbelievers: they hear sounds, but they do not listen with acceptance, understanding and obedience. As the Most High says:

“The example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts at what hears nothing but calls and cries.”

Likewise, it does not follow that all ordinary hearing—all forms of hearing—must be ruled out for the dead used in this comparison, just as this was not ruled out for the disbelievers. Rather, what is absent in their case is the ordinary hearing from which they would benefit; other hearing is not ruled out for them.

original_text:
وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحَيْنِ وَغَيْرِهِمَا أَنَّ الْمَيِّتَ يَسْمَعُ خَفْقَ نِعَالِهِمْ إذَا وَلَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ فَهَذَا مُوَافِقٌ لِهَذَا فَكَيْفَ يَدْفَعُ ذَلِكَ؟
 وَمِنْ الْعُلَمَاءِ مَنْ قَالَ:
 إنَّ الْمَيِّتَ فِي قَبْرِهِ لَا يَسْمَعُ مَا دَامَ مَيِّتًا كَمَا قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ.
 وَاسْتَدَلَّتْ بِهِ مِنْ الْقُرْآنِ وَأَمَّا إذَا أَحْيَاهُ اللَّهُ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْمَعُ كَمَا قَالَ قتادة:
 أَحْيَاهُمْ اللَّهُ لَهُ. وَإِنْ كَانَتْ تِلْكَ الْحَيَاةُ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا كَمَا نَحْنُ لَا نَرَى الْمَلَائِكَةَ وَالْجِنَّ وَلَا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُحِسُّ بِهِ الْمَيِّتُ فِي مَنَامِهِ وَكَمَا لَا يَعْلَمُ الْإِنْسَانُ مَا فِي قَلْبِ الْآخَرِ وَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ يَعْلَمُ ذَلِكَ مَنْ أَطْلَعَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ. وَهَذِهِ جُمْلَةٌ يَحْصُلُ بِهَا مَقْصُودُ السَّائِلِ وَإِنْ كَانَ لَهَا مِنْ الشَّرْحِ وَالتَّفْصِيلِ مَا لَيْسَ هَذَا مَوْضِعَهُ فَإِنَّ مَا ذَكَرْنَاهُ مِنْ الْأَدِلَّةِ الْبَيِّنَةِ عَلَى مَا سَأَلَ عَنْهُ مَا لَا يَكَادُ مَجْمُوعًا. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ وَسَلَّمَ.
translated_text:
It is also established in the two Sahīh collections and elsewhere that the deceased hears the sound of their sandals as they turn and walk away. This accords with what has been stated, so how can it be rejected?

Some scholars hold that the deceased does not hear in his grave so long as he remains dead, as ‘Ā’ishah stated, citing evidence from the Quran. If Allah brings him to life, however, he hears, as Qatādah said: “Allah brought them to life for that purpose.” Even if they do not hear through that life, just as we do not see the angels and jinn, we do not know what the deceased experiences in his sleep. Likewise, a person does not know what is in another’s heart, although someone to whom Allah has disclosed it may know it.

This is a summary sufficient to answer the questioner’s inquiry, although further explanation and detail would be beyond the scope of this discussion. For the clear evidence we have cited concerning his question is rarely gathered together. Allah knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad, his family and his Companions, and grant them peace.

قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ - قَدَّسَ اللَّهُ رُوحَهُ -:
سَأَلَ سَائِلٌ:
 بِمَاذَا يُخَاطَبُ النَّاسُ يَوْمَ الْبَعْثِ؟ وَهَلْ يُخَاطِبُهُمْ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِلِسَانِ الْعَرَبِ؟ وَهَلْ يَصِحُّ أَنَّ لِسَانَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ الْفَارِسِيَّةُ وَأَنَّ لِسَانَ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ
فَأَجَبْته بَعْدَ:
الْحَمْدِ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، لَا يُعْلَمُ بِأَيِّ لُغَةٍ يَتَكَلَّمُ النَّاسُ يَوْمَئِذٍ وَلَا بِأَيِّ لُغَةٍ يَسْمَعُونَ خِطَابَ الرَّبِّ جَلَّ وَعَلَا؛ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى لَمْ يُخْبِرْنَا بِشَيْءِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا رَسُولُهُ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ وَلَمْ يَصِحَّ أَنَّ الْفَارِسِيَّةَ لُغَةُ الجهنميين وَلَا أَنَّ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ لُغَةُ أَهْلِ النَّعِيمِ الْأَبَدِيِّ وَلَا نَعْلَمُ نِزَاعًا فِي ذَلِكَ بَيْنَ الصَّحَابَةِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ بَلْ كُلُّهُمْ يَكُفُّونَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ الْكَلَامَ فِي مِثْلِ هَذَا مِنْ فُضُولِ الْقَوْلِ وَلَا قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى لِأَصْحَابِ الثَّرَى وَلَكِنْ حَدَثَ فِي ذَلِكَ خِلَافٌ بَيْنَ الْمُتَأَخِّرِينَ.
 فَقَالَ نَاسٌ:
 يَتَخَاطَبُونَ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ. وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ إلَّا أَهْلَ النَّارِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُجِيبُونَ بِالْفَارِسِيَّةِ وَهِيَ لُغَتُهُمْ فِي النَّارِ.
translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah sanctify his soul—said:

Someone asked: “In what language will people be addressed on the Day of Resurrection? Will Allah Most High address them in Arabic? Is it true that the language of the people of Hell is Persian and that the language of the people of Paradise is Arabic?”

After saying, “Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds,” I answered him:

It is not known what language people will speak that day, nor in what language they will hear the address of the Lord, Glorious and Exalted. Neither Allah Most High nor His Messenger—peace and blessings be upon him—has informed us of any of this. It has not been authentically established that Persian is the language of the people of Hell, or that Arabic is the language of those enjoying eternal bliss. We know of no disagreement concerning this among the Companions—may Allah be pleased with them. Rather, they all refrained from discussing it, because speaking about such matters is superfluous talk; nor did Allah Most High say anything concerning this to the people of the earth. However, disagreement on this matter arose among later generations.

Some said: “They will converse in Arabic.” Others said: “Except for the people of Hell: they will reply in Persian, which is their language in Hell.”

original_text:
وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ:
 يَتَخَاطَبُونَ بِالسُّرْيانِيَّةِ لِأَنَّهَا لُغَةُ آدَمَ وَعَنْهَا تَفَرَّعَتْ اللُّغَاتُ.
 وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ:
 إلَّا أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ. وَكُلُّ هَذِهِ الْأَقْوَالِ لَا حُجَّةَ لِأَرْبَابِهَا لَا مِنْ طَرِيقِ عَقْلٍ وَلَا نَقْلٍ بَلْ هِيَ دَعَاوَى عَارِيَةٌ عَنْ الْأَدِلَّةِ وَاَللَّهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى أَعْلَمُ وَأَحْكَمُ.
translated_text:
And others said: “They will converse in Syriac, because it was the language of Adam, from which the other languages branched out.”

Others said: “Except for the people of Paradise, who will speak Arabic.”

The proponents of all these views have no proof for them, whether rational or transmitted. Rather, these are claims devoid of evidence. Allah, Glorious and Exalted, knows best and is most wise.

He was asked:
“Does the Scale mean justice, or does it have two pans?”

He replied:
“The Scale” is that by which deeds are weighed; it is distinct from justice, as the Quran and Sunnah indicate. For example, Allah Most High says:
“Whoever’s scales are heavy,”
and:
“Whoever’s scales are light.”
He also says:
“We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection.”

In the two Sahīh collections, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is reported to have said:
“Two phrases are light on the tongue, heavy in the Scale, and beloved to the Most Merciful: ‘Glory and praise be to Allah; glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.’”

He also said of the two legs of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd:
“They are heavier in the Scale than Mount Uhud.”

Al-Tirmidhī and others relate the hadith of the card, which al-Tirmidhī, al-Hākim, and others graded authentic. It concerns a man who is brought forward, and ninety-nine records are spread out for him, each extending as far as the eye can see. They are placed in one pan, and a card is brought for him bearing the testimony that none is worthy of worship except Allah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
“Then the records proved light, and the card heavy.”

This and similar reports make clear that deeds are weighed in scales that show whether good deeds outweigh evil deeds or vice versa. The Scale is thus the means by which justice becomes manifest. The purpose of weighing is justice, as with the scales of this world. As for the precise nature of those scales, it is on the same footing as the nature of all the other matters of the unseen about which we have been told.

 وَأَطْفَالُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ}
 
".

 "

{أَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِي عَرَصَاتِ الْقِيَامَةِ يُؤْمَرُونَ وَيُنْهَوْنَ فَمَنْ أَطَاعَ دَخَلَ الْجَنَّةَ وَمَنْ عَصَى دَخَلَ النَّارَ}
 . وَهَذَا هُوَ الَّذِي ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ أَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ. وَالتَّكْلِيفُ إنَّمَا يَنْقَطِعُ بِدُخُولِ دَارِ الْجَزَاءِ وَهِيَ الْجَنَّةُ وَالنَّارُ.
translated_text:
The shaykh said:

Regarding the children of unbelievers, the soundest view is:
“Allah knows best what they would have done.”

This was the answer given by the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in an authentic hadith. A group of hadith scholars and others said that they are all in Hell. This has been cited as one of Ahmad’s explicit statements, but it is wrongly attributed to him. Another group asserted that they are all in Paradise. Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī and others adopted this view, citing as evidence a hadith that relates:

“In a dream, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw Abraham, the close friend of Allah, with the children of the believers beside him. He was asked, ‘O Messenger of Allah, and the children of the polytheists?’ He replied, ‘And the children of the polytheists.’”

The correct position is to say:
“Allah knows best what they would have done.”

We do not judge any particular child among them to be destined for either Paradise or Hell. Several hadiths relate:
“On the Day of Resurrection, in the gathering grounds, they will be given commands and prohibitions. Whoever obeys will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys will enter Hell.”

This is the position that Abū al-Hasan al-Ashʿarī reported from Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah. Being subject to divine commands ends only upon entering the abode of recompense: Paradise or Hell.

{يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ وَيُدْعَوْنَ إلَى السُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ}

 } الْآيَةَ. وَالْكَلَامُ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْأُمُورِ مَبْسُوطٌ فِي غَيْرِ هَذَا الْمَوْضِعِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
As for the gathering grounds on the Day of Resurrection, they will be tested there, just as they are tested in the barzakh (the intermediate state). One of them is asked:

“Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?”

Allah Most High says in the verse:

“On the Day when a shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostrate, but will not be able to.”

The hadith concerning Allah manifesting Himself to His servants at the gathering has been established through several chains of transmission in the authentic hadith collections. It relates what happens when it is said:

“‘Let every people follow what they used to worship.’ The polytheists follow their gods, while the believers remain. Then the Lord manifests Himself to them in a form other than the one they recognize, and they do not recognize Him. Then He manifests Himself to them in the form they recognize, and the believers prostrate to Him. The hypocrites’ backs, however, remain stiff like cattle’s horns: they wish to prostrate but cannot. He also mentioned His words in the verse: ‘On the Day when a shin will be uncovered and they will be called to prostrate, but will not be able to.’”

These matters are discussed at length elsewhere. And Allah knows best.

 تَنَازَعَ فِيهَا الْمُتَأَخِّرُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَحْمَدَ وَغَيْرِهِمْ فَمِمَّنْ قَالَ إنَّهُمْ لَا يُحَاسَبُونَ: أَبُو بَكْرٍ عَبْدُ الْعَزِيزِ وَأَبُو الْحَسَنِ التَّمِيمِيُّ وَالْقَاضِي أَبُو يَعْلَى وَغَيْرُهُمْ وَمِمَّنْ قَالَ: إنَّهُمْ يُحَاسَبُونَ: أَبُو حَفْصٍ الْبَرْمَكِيُّ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَحْمَدَ وَأَبُو سُلَيْمَانَ الدِّمَشْقِيُّ وَأَبُو طَالِبٍ الْمَكِّيُّ. وَفَصْلُ الْخِطَابِ أَنَّ الْحِسَابَ يُرَادُ بِهِ عَرْضُ أَعْمَالِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَتَوْبِيخُهُمْ عَلَيْهَا وَيُرَادُ بِالْحِسَابِ مُوَازَنَةُ الْحَسَنَاتِ بِالسَّيِّئَاتِ. فَإِنْ أُرِيدَ بِالْحِسَابِ الْمَعْنَى الْأَوَّلُ فَلَا رَيْبَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحَاسَبُونَ بِهَذَا الِاعْتِبَارِ. وَإِنْ أُرِيدَ الْمَعْنَى الثَّانِي فَإِنْ قُصِدَ بِذَلِكَ أَنَّ الْكُفَّارَ تَبْقَى لَهُمْ حَسَنَاتٌ يَسْتَحِقُّونَ بِهَا الْجَنَّةَ فَهَذَا خَطَأٌ ظَاهِرٌ. وَإِنْ أُرِيدَ أَنَّهُمْ يَتَفَاوَتُونَ فِي الْعِقَابِ؛ فَعِقَابُ مَنْ كَثُرَتْ سَيِّئَاتُهُ أَعْظَمُ مِنْ
translated_text:
He was asked about the disbelievers:
“Will they be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection or not?”

He replied:

This “question” has been disputed by later scholars among Ahmad’s followers and others. Those who said that they will not be brought to account include Abū Bakr Abd al-Azīz, Abū al-Hasan al-Tamīmī, al-Qādī Abū Ya'lā, and others. Those who said that they will be brought to account include Abū Hafs al-Barmakī, one of Ahmad’s followers, Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī, and Abū Tālib al-Makkī.

The decisive distinction is that “reckoning” may mean having their deeds presented to them and being rebuked for them, or it may mean weighing good deeds against evil deeds. If reckoning is understood in the first sense, there is no doubt that they will be brought to account in this respect. If it is understood in the second sense, and what is intended is that the disbelievers retain good deeds by which they deserve Paradise, this is plainly mistaken. But if what is meant is that their punishments differ in severity, then the punishment of those whose evil deeds are more numerous is greater than

that of those whose evil deeds are fewer; those who have good deeds will have their punishment lightened, just as Abū Tālib’s punishment is lighter than Abū Lahab’s.

Allah Most High says:

“Those who disbelieved and hindered others from Allah’s path—We will increase their punishment upon punishment.”

And He says:

“Postponement of the sacred months is only an increase in disbelief.”

Hell has descending levels. Thus, if some disbelievers suffer more severe punishment than others—because their evil deeds are more numerous and their good deeds fewer—then the reckoning serves to determine the degrees of punishment, not to admit them to Paradise.

فَأَجَابَ:
لَا يَكْفُرُ بِمُجَرَّدِ الذَّنْبِ فَإِنَّهُ ثَبَتَ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَإِجْمَاعِ السَّلَفِ أَنَّ الزَّانِيَ غَيْرَ الْمُحْصَنِ يُجْلَدُ وَلَا يُقْتَلُ وَالشَّارِبُ يُجْلَدُ وَالْقَاذِفُ يُجْلَدُ وَالسَّارِقُ يُقْطَعُ. وَلَوْ كَانُوا كُفَّارًا لَكَانُوا مُرْتَدِّينَ وَوَجَبَ قَتْلُهُمْ وَهَذَا خِلَافُ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَإِجْمَاعِ السَّلَفِ.
translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām Abū al-ʿAbbās Taqī al-Dīn ibn Taymiyyah—may Allah sanctify his soul—was asked:

“Does a believing servant become a disbeliever by committing a sin, or not?”

He replied:

He does not become a disbeliever merely by committing a sin. For the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations establish that a person who commits unlawful sexual intercourse without having consummated a valid marriage is flogged, not put to death; one who drinks intoxicants is flogged; one who makes an unsubstantiated accusation of unlawful sexual intercourse is flogged; and a thief has his hand amputated. If they were disbelievers, they would be apostates, and putting them to death would be obligatory. This, however, contradicts the Quran, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the early generations.

فَأَجَابَ:
إنْ تَابَ عَنْ ذُنُوبِهِ تَوْبَةً نَصُوحًا، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ لَهُ وَلَا يَحْرِمُهُ مَا كَانَ وَعَدَهُ؛ بَلْ يُعْطِيه ذَلِكَ. وَإِنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ وُزِنَتْ حَسَنَاتُهُ وَسَيِّئَاتُهُ فَإِنْ رَجَحَتْ حَسَنَاتُهُ عَلَى سَيِّئَاتِهِ كَانَ مَنْ أَهْلِ الثَّوَابِ وَإِنْ رَجَحَتْ سَيِّئَاتُهُ عَلَى حَسَنَاتِهِ كَانَ مَنْ أَهْلِ الْعَذَابِ.
 وَمَا أُعِدَّ لَهُ مِنْ الثَّوَابِ يُحْبَطُ حِينَئِذٍ بِالسَّيِّئَاتِ الَّتِي زَادَتْ عَلَى حَسَنَاتِهِ كَمَا أَنَّهُ إذَا عَمِلَ سَيِّئَاتٍ اسْتَحَقَّ بِهَا النَّارَ ثُمَّ عَمِلَ بَعْدَهَا حَسَنَاتٍ:
 تَذْهَبُ السَّيِّئَاتُ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

“A Muslim man performs a deed that merits having a palace built for him in Paradise and plantings made in his name. He then commits sins for which he deserves Hell. If he enters Hell, how can he be listed as being in Paradise while he is in Hell?”

He replied:

If he sincerely repents of his sins, Allah will forgive him and will not deprive him of what He had promised him; rather, He will grant it to him. If he does not repent, his good and evil deeds will be weighed. If his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds, he will be among those rewarded; if his evil deeds outweigh his good deeds, he will be among those punished.

The reward prepared for him is then nullified by the evil deeds that outweighed his good deeds. Likewise, if he commits evil deeds for which he deserves Hell, then afterwards performs good deeds, those evil deeds are erased. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He was asked about intercession for “those who commit major sins” among the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and whether they will enter Paradise.

He replied:

The hadiths concerning intercession for “those who commit major sins” are firmly established and mass-transmitted from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The righteous predecessors—the Companions and those who followed them in righteousness—and the leading scholars of the Muslims have agreed upon them. Only the adherents of religious innovation, such as the Khawārij, the Mu‘tazila, and others like them, have disputed this.

No one with an atom’s weight of faith in his heart will remain in Hell. Rather, they will all emerge from Hell and enter Paradise, and there will still be room left in Paradise. Allah will then create other beings for it and admit them to Paradise, as is established in an authentic hadith from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

translated_text:
He was also asked:

Will “the children of the believers” remain as they were when they died, or will they grow up and marry? Will the girls also marry?

The answer:

Praise be to Allah. When they enter Paradise, they will enter it just as adults do, in the form of their father Adam, sixty cubits tall and seven cubits wide. They will marry just as adults do. Any woman who dies without having married will be married in the Hereafter. Likewise, any man who dies will marry in the Hereafter. And Allah Most High knows best.

translated_text:
The shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Do the people of Paradise have offspring? And the “young boys”—are they the children of the people of Paradise? What is the fate of children? When the souls of the people of Paradise and Hell leave the body, are they in Paradise enjoying bliss, or do they remain in a particular place until Allah resurrects the body? What is the fate of a child born of fornication who dies: will he be among the people of the Heights or in Paradise? What is the correct view regarding the children of polytheists: are they among the people of Hell or the people of Paradise? Are the days in the Hereafter named as they are in this world, such as Saturday and Sunday?

He replied:

The “young boys” who go about attending to the people of Paradise are among the creatures of Paradise; they are not the children of people from this world. Rather, when children from this world enter Paradise, their physical form is perfected like that of the people of Paradise: in the form of Adam, thirty-three years of age and sixty cubits tall. It has also been reported that they are seven cubits wide.

The souls of the believers are in Paradise, and the souls of the disbelievers are in Hell. The souls of the believers enjoy bliss, while the souls of the disbelievers suffer punishment, until they are restored to their bodies.

 ". وَدَلَّتْ الْأَحَادِيثُ الصَّحِيحَةُ أَنَّ بَعْضَهُمْ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَبَعْضَهُمْ فِي النَّارِ. وَالْجَنَّةُ لَيْسَ فِيهَا شَمْسٌ وَلَا قَمَرٌ وَلَا لَيْلٌ وَلَا نَهَارٌ لَكِنْ تُعْرَفُ الْبُكْرَةُ وَالْعَشِيَّةُ بِنُورِ يَظْهَرُ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْعَرْشِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
And if a “child born of fornication” believes and does righteous deeds, he will enter Paradise; otherwise, he will be recompensed for his deeds just as anyone else is. Recompense is based on deeds, not lineage. A child born of fornication is censured only because he is likely to commit evil deeds, as often happens, just as noble lineages are praised because they are likely to foster good deeds. Once a person’s deeds become evident, however, recompense is based on them. The most honored of all creatures in Allah’s sight are the most righteous.

As for “the children of polytheists,” the soundest answer concerning them is the answer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as related in the two Sahīh collections:

“Every child is born upon the natural disposition”—and the rest of the hadith.

He was asked, “O Messenger of Allah, what about the children of polytheists who die while still young?” He replied, “Allah knows best what they would have done.”

Thus, no particular child among them is judged to be destined for either Paradise or Hell. It is narrated:

“On the Day of Resurrection, they will be tested on the plains of the Resurrection. Whoever obeys Allah then will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys will enter Hell.”

Authentic hadiths indicate that some of them will be in Paradise and some in Hell.

In Paradise there is neither sun nor moon, neither night nor day. Morning and evening, however, are known by a light that appears from the direction of the Throne. And Allah knows best.

original_text:
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ قِيلَ لَهُ:
 إنَّهُ وَرَدَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ 
" 
{أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْجَنَّةِ يَأْكُلُونَ وَيَشْرَبُونَ وَيَتَمَتَّعُونَ وَلَا يَبُولُونَ وَلَا يَتَغَوَّطُونَ}
 "
 فَقَالَ: مَنْ أَكَلَ وَشَرِبَ: بَالَ وَتَغَوَّطَ.
 ثُمَّ قِيلَ لَهُ:
 إنَّ فِي الْجَنَّةِ طُيُورًا إذَا اشْتَهَى صَارَ قُدَّامَهُ عَلَى أَيِّ صُورَةٍ أَرَادَ مِنْ الْأَطْعِمَةِ وَغَيْرِهَا فَقَالَ: هَذَا فَشَّارٌ. هَلْ بِجَحْدِهِ هَذَا يَكْفُرُ وَيَجِبُ قَتْلُهُ أَمْ لَا؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْأَكْلُ وَالشُّرْبُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ ثَابِتٌ بِكِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَسُنَّةِ رَسُولِهِ وَإِجْمَاعِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ.
 وَهُوَ مَعْلُومٌ بِالِاضْطِرَارِ مِنْ دِينِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَكَذَلِكَ الطُّيُورُ وَالْقُصُورُ فِي الْجَنَّةِ بِلَا رَيْبٍ كَمَا وُصِفَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْأَحَادِيثِ الصَّحِيحَةِ الثَّابِتَةِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَكَذَلِكَ إنَّ أَهْلَ الْجَنَّةِ لَا يَبُولُونَ وَلَا يَتَغَوَّطُونَ وَلَا يَبْصُقُونَ لَمْ يُخَالِفْ مِنْ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بِاَللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ أَحَدٌ وَإِنَّمَا الْمُخَالِفُ فِي ذَلِكَ أَحَدُ رَجُلَيْنِ:
 إمَّا كَافِرٌ وَإِمَّا مُنَافِقٌ. أَمَّا الْكَافِرُ فَإِنَّ الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصَارَى يُنْكِرُونَ الْأَكْلَ وَالشُّرْبَ وَالنِّكَاحَ فِي
translated_text:
And he—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about a man who was told that it had been reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The inhabitants of Paradise eat, drink, and enjoy themselves, but neither urinate nor defecate.”

He replied, “Whoever eats and drinks urinates and defecates.” Then he was told, “There are birds in Paradise which, whenever one desires them, appear before him in whatever form he wishes, as food or otherwise.” He replied, “This is nonsense.” Does his denial of this make him a disbeliever and necessitate his execution, or not?

He answered:

Eating and drinking in Paradise are established by the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the consensus of the Muslims. This is something necessarily known to be part of the religion of Islam. Likewise, there are undoubtedly birds and palaces in Paradise, as described in the authentic hadiths established from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Similarly, the inhabitants of Paradise neither urinate, defecate, nor spit. No believer in Allah and His Messenger has disagreed with this. Anyone who disagrees is one of two kinds: either a disbeliever or a hypocrite. As for the disbeliever, the Jews and Christians deny eating, drinking, and sexual relations in

original_text:
الْجَنَّةِ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْجَنَّةِ إنَّمَا يَتَمَتَّعُونَ بِالْأَصْوَاتِ الْمُطْرِبَةِ وَالْأَرْوَاحِ الطَّيِّبَةِ مَعَ نَعِيمِ الْأَرْوَاحِ وَهُمْ يُقِرُّونَ مَعَ ذَلِكَ بِحَشْرِ الْأَجْسَادِ مَعَ الْأَرْوَاحِ وَنَعِيمِهَا وَعَذَابِهَا. وَأَمَّا طَوَائِفُ مِنْ الْكُفَّار وَغَيْرِهِمْ مِنْ الصَّابِئَةِ وَالْفَلَاسِفَةِ وَمَنْ وَافَقَهُمْ فَيُقِرُّونَ بِحَشْرِ الْأَرْوَاحِ فَقَطْ وَأَنَّ النَّعِيمَ وَالْعَذَابَ لِلْأَرْوَاحِ فَقَطْ. وَطَوَائِفُ مِنْ الْكُفَّار وَالْمُشْرِكِينَ وَغَيْرِهِمْ يُنْكِرُونَ الْمَعَادَ بِالْكُلِّيَّةِ فَلَا يُقِرُّونَ لَا بِمَعَادِ الْأَرْوَاحِ؛ وَلَا الْأَجْسَادِ. وَقَدْ بَيَّنَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ عَلَى لِسَانِ رَسُولِهِ أَمْرَ مَعَادِ الْأَرْوَاحِ وَالْأَجْسَادِ وَرَدَّ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ وَالْمُنْكِرِينَ لِشَيْءِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بَيَانًا فِي غَايَةِ التَّمَامِ وَالْكَمَالِ.
 وَأَمَّا الْمُنَافِقُونَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْأُمَّةِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُقِرُّونَ بِأَلْفَاظِ الْقُرْآنِ وَالسُّنَّةِ الْمَشْهُورَةِ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ وَيَقُولُونَ هَذِهِ أَمْثَالٌ ضُرِبَتْ لِنَفْهَمَ الْمَعَادَ الرُّوحَانِيَّ وَهَؤُلَاءِ مِثْلُ الْقَرَامِطَةِ الْبَاطِنِيَّةِ الَّذِينَ قَوْلُهُمْ مُؤَلَّفٌ مِنْ قَوْلِ الْمَجُوسِ وَالصَّابِئَةِ وَمِثْلُ الْمُتَفَلْسِفَةِ الصَّابِئَةِ الْمُنْتَسِبِينَ إلَى الْإِسْلَامِ وَطَائِفَةٍ مِمَّنْ ضَاهُوهُمْ:
 مِنْ كَاتِبٍ أَوْ مُتَطَبِّبٍ أَوْ مُتَكَلِّمٍ أَوْ مُتَصَوِّفٍ كَأَصْحَابِ 
" رَسَائِلِ إخْوَانِ الصَّفَا "
 وَغَيْرِهِمْ أَوْ مُنَافِقٌ. وَهَؤُلَاءِ كُلُّهُمْ كُفَّارٌ يَجِبُ قَتْلُهُمْ بِاتِّفَاقِ أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ؛ فَإِنَّ مُحَمَّدًا صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَدّ بَيَّنَ ذَلِكَ بَيَانًا شَافِيًا قَاطِعًا لِلْعُذْرِ
translated_text:
Paradise, claiming that its inhabitants enjoy only delightful sounds and pleasant scents, together with the bliss experienced by their souls. Nevertheless, they acknowledge the resurrection of bodies together with souls, and their bliss and torment. Certain groups of disbelievers and others—Sabians, philosophers, and those who agree with them—acknowledge only the resurrection of souls, holding that bliss and torment affect souls alone. Other groups of disbelievers, polytheists, and others deny the resurrection altogether, acknowledging the resurrection of neither souls nor bodies. In His Book, through His Messenger, Allah Most High has explained the resurrection of souls and bodies and refuted the disbelievers and those who deny any part of it, with an explanation of the utmost completeness and perfection.

As for the hypocrites of this community who do not acknowledge the well-known wording of the Quran and Sunnah, they distort words from their proper meanings and say, “These are examples given to help us understand the spiritual resurrection.” These include the esoteric Qarmatians, whose doctrine combines the teachings of the Magians and the Sabians; the Sabian adherents of philosophy who profess Islam; and groups who resemble them: writers, physicians, theologians, or Sufis, such as the authors of Rasā’il Ikhwān al-Safā (Epistles of the Brethren of Purity) and others—or a hypocrite. All of these are disbelievers who must be put to death, by the consensus of the people of faith; for Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has explained this fully and conclusively, leaving no excuse

and this has been transmitted through numerous independent channels among his community, both its learned members and the general populace. One of the Jews debated him on a question of this kind, saying:

“O Muhammad, you say that the people of Paradise eat and drink, but whoever eats and drinks must relieve himself.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, replied, “Perspiration like musk.”

It is incumbent upon the ruler to put to death anyone who denies this, even if he outwardly affirms its wording. What, then, of someone who denies it all? Allah knows best.

سُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
هَلْ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ يَأْكُلُونَ وَيَشْرَبُونَ وَيَنْكِحُونَ بِتَلَذُّذِ كَالدُّنْيَا؟ وَهَلْ تُبْعَثُ هَذِهِ الْأَجْسَامُ بِعَيْنِهَا؟ وَهَلْ عِيسَى حَيٌّ أَمْ مَيِّتٌ؟ وَهَلْ إذَا نَزَلَ يَحْكُمُ بِشَرِيعَةِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَمْ بِشَرِيعَتِهِ الْأُولَى أَمْ تُحْدَثُ لَهُ شَرِيعَةٌ؟
فَأَجَابَ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ -:
أَمَّا أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ فَيَأْكُلُونَ وَيَشْرَبُونَ وَيَنْكِحُونَ مُتَنَعِّمِينَ بِذَلِكَ بِإِجْمَاعِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ كَمَا نَطَقَ بِهِ الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ وَإِنَّمَا يُنْكِرُ ذَلِكَ مَنْ يُنْكِرُهُ مِنْ الْيَهُودِ وَالنَّصَارَى. وَهَذِهِ الْأَجْسَادُ هِيَ الَّتِي تُبْعَثُ كَمَا نَطَقَ بِهِ الْكِتَابُ وَالسُّنَّةُ. وَعِيسَى حَيٌّ فِي السَّمَاءِ لَمْ يَمُتْ بَعْدُ. وَإِذَا نَزَلَ مِنْ السَّمَاءِ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ إلَّا بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ؛ لَا بِشَيْءِ يُخَالِفُ ذَلِكَ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“Do the people of Paradise eat, drink, and have sexual relations with pleasure as in this world? Will these very bodies be resurrected? Is Jesus alive or dead? When he descends, will he judge according to the law of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, according to his own earlier law, or will a new law be instituted for him?”

He—may Allah be pleased with him—answered:

The people of Paradise eat, drink, and have sexual relations, enjoying all of these, according to the consensus of the Muslims, as explicitly stated in the Quran and the Sunnah. The only people who deny this are those among the Jews and Christians who do so. These same bodies will be resurrected, as explicitly stated in the Quran and the Sunnah. Jesus is alive in heaven and has not yet died. When he descends from heaven, he will judge only according to the Quran and the Sunnah, not by anything that contradicts them. Allah knows best.

وَأَفْضَلُ

" إبْرَاهِيمُ الْخَلِيلُ "
 كَمَا ثَبَتَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَنَسٍ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ

 "
.
 وَكَذَلِكَ قَالَ الْعُلَمَاءُ:
 مِنْهُمْ الرَّبِيعُ بْنُ خُثَيْم قَالَ: لَا أُفَضِّلُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا أَحَدًا وَلَا أُفَضِّلُ عَلَى إبْرَاهِيمَ بَعْدَ نَبِيِّنَا أَحَدًا.
original_footnote: (١) في المطبوعة " خيثم " والمثبت من كتب الرجال
translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah sanctify his soul—said:

Section:

The greatest of the “prophets” after Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is “Abraham, Allah’s close friend,” as established in Sahīh Muslim through Anas’s report from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that “he is the best of creation.”

The scholars likewise stated this. Among them was al-Rabī‘ ibn Khuthaym, who said: “I place no one above our Prophet, and after our Prophet, I place no one above Abraham.”
translated_footnote: (1) The printed edition reads “Khaytham”; the reading adopted here follows the biographical dictionaries of hadith transmitters.

original_text:
سُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
فِيمَنْ يَقُولُ:
 إنَّ غَيْرَ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ يَبْلُغُ دَرَجَتَهُمْ بِحَيْثُ يَأْمَنُونَ مَكْرَ اللَّهِ هَلْ يَأْثَمُ بِهَذَا الِاعْتِقَادِ؟.
فَأَجَابَ:
مَنْ اعْتَقَدَ أَنَّ فِي أَوْلِيَاءِ اللَّهِ مَنْ لَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ اتِّبَاعُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ وَطَاعَتُهُمْ فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ يُسْتَتَابُ فَإِنْ تَابَ وَإِلَّا قُتِلَ مِثْلُ مَنْ يَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ فِي أُمَّةِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مَنْ يَسْتَغْنِي عَنْ مُتَابَعَتِهِ كَمَا اسْتَغْنَى الْخَضِرُ عَنْ مُتَابَعَةِ مُوسَى فَإِنَّ مُوسَى لَمْ تَكُنْ دَعْوَتُهُ عَامَّةً بِخِلَافِ مُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَإِنَّهُ مَبْعُوثٌ إلَى كُلِّ أَحَدٍ فَيَجِبُ عَلَى كُلِّ أَحَدٍ مُتَابَعَةُ أَمْرِهِ وَإِذَا كَانَ مَنْ اعْتَقَدَ سُقُوطَ طَاعَتِهِ عَنْهُ كَافِرًا؛ فَكَيْفَ مَنْ اعْتَقَدَ أَنَّهُ أَفْضَلُ مِنْهُ؟ أَوْ أَنَّهُ يَصِيرُ مِثْلَهُ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ اعْتَقَدَ أَنَّ مِنْ الْأَوْلِيَاءِ مَنْ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ كَمَا بُشِّرَ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ بِالْجَنَّةِ وَكَمَا قَدْ يُعَرِّفُ اللَّهُ بَعْضَ الْأَوْلِيَاءِ أَنَّهُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ فَهَذَا لَا يَكْفُرُ. وَمَعَ هَذَا فَلَا بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

“Is someone sinful for believing that those who are not prophets can attain the rank of the prophets, to the point that they feel secure from Allah’s devising?”

He replied:

Whoever believes that among the friends of Allah there are those who are not obliged to follow and obey the messengers is an unbeliever. He must be called upon to repent; if he repents, so be it; otherwise, he is to be put to death. This includes someone who believes that among the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, there are those who have no need to follow him, just as al-Khidr had no need to follow Moses. Moses’s mission was not universal, unlike that of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who was sent to everyone. Everyone is therefore obliged to follow his commands. If someone who believes that he is exempt from obeying him is an unbeliever, then what of someone who believes that he is superior to him, or that he can become his equal?

As for someone who believes that certain friends of Allah know that they are among the people of Paradise—just as a number of the Companions were given glad tidings of Paradise, and just as Allah may make known to some of His friends that they are among its people—he is not an unbeliever on that account. Even so, he must still fear Allah Most High. And Allah knows best.

سُئِلَ الشَّيْخُ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَالَ:
 إنَّ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ عَلَيْهِمْ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ مَعْصُومُونَ مِنْ الْكَبَائِرِ دُونَ الصَّغَائِرِ فَكَفَّرَهُ رَجُلٌ بِهَذِهِ فَهَلْ قَائِلُ ذَلِكَ مُخْطِئٌ أَوْ مُصِيبٌ؟ وَهَلْ قَالَ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ بِعِصْمَةِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ مُطْلَقًا؟ وَمَا الصَّوَابُ فِي ذَلِكَ؟.
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، لَيْسَ هُوَ كَافِرًا بِاتِّفَاقِ أَهْلِ الدِّينِ وَلَا هَذَا مِنْ مَسَائِلِ السَّبِّ الْمُتَنَازَعِ فِي اسْتِتَابَةِ قَائِلِهِ بِلَا نِزَاعٍ كَمَا صَرَّحَ بِذَلِكَ الْقَاضِي عِيَاضٌ وَأَمْثَالُهُ مَعَ مُبَالَغَتِهِمْ فِي الْقَوْلِ بِالْعِصْمَةِ وَفِي عُقُوبَةِ السَّابِّ؛ وَمَعَ هَذَا فَهُمْ مُتَّفِقُونَ عَلَى أَنَّ الْقَوْلَ بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ لَيْسَ هُوَ مِنْ مَسَائِلِ السَّبِّ وَالْعُقُوبَةِ فَضْلًا أَنْ يَكُونَ قَائِلُ ذَلِكَ كَافِرًا أَوْ فَاسِقًا؛ فَإِنَّ الْقَوْلَ بِأَنَّ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ مَعْصُومُونَ عَنْ الْكَبَائِرِ دُونَ الصَّغَائِرِ هُوَ قَوْلُ أَكْثَرِ عُلَمَاءِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَجَمِيعِ الطَّوَائِفِ حَتَّى إنَّهُ قَوْلُ أَكْثَرِ أَهْلِ الْكَلَامِ كَمَا ذَكَرَ 
" أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الآمدي "
 أَنَّ هَذَا قَوْلُ أَكْثَرِ الْأَشْعَرِيَّةِ وَهُوَ أَيْضًا قَوْلُ أَكْثَرِ أَهْلِ التَّفْسِيرِ وَالْحَدِيثِ وَالْفُقَهَاءِ بَلْ هُوَ لَمْ يَنْقُلْ عَنْ السَّلَفِ وَالْأَئِمَّةِ وَالصَّحَابَةِ وَالتَّابِعِينَ وَتَابِعِيهِمْ إلَّا مَا يُوَافِقُ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ وَلَمْ يَنْقُلْ عَنْهُمْ مَا يُوَافِقُ الْقَوْلَ. . . 
(١)

translated_text:
The Shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“A man said that the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, are protected from major sins but not minor sins. Another man declared him an unbeliever for saying this. Is the person who said this mistaken or correct? Has any of them maintained that the prophets are protected from sin without qualification? What is the correct position on this?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. By agreement of the scholars of the religion, he is not an unbeliever. There is likewise no disagreement that this does not fall under those cases of insulting the prophets in which scholars dispute whether the speaker should be called upon to repent. Al-Qādī ‘Iyād and others like him explicitly stated this, despite their stringent positions on prophetic protection from sin and the punishment of those who insult the prophets. Nevertheless, they agree that such a statement does not fall under the rulings concerning insult and punishment, let alone render its speaker an unbeliever or a flagrant sinner.

Indeed, the view that the prophets are protected from major sins but not minor sins is held by the majority of Islamic scholars across all groups. It is even the position of most speculative theologians: “Abū al-Hasan al-Āmidī” mentioned that this is the view of most Ash‘arīs. It is also the position of most scholars of Quranic exegesis and hadith, and most jurists. Indeed, only reports consistent with this view have been transmitted from the early generations, the leading scholars, the Companions, the Successors, and their followers; no reports have been transmitted from them consistent with the view . . . (1)

وَإِنَّمَا نُقِلَ ذَلِكَ الْقَوْلَ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْمُتَقَدِّمِ عَنْ الرَّافِضَةِ ثُمَّ عَنْ بَعْضِ الْمُعْتَزِلَةِ ثُمَّ وَافَقَهُمْ عَلَيْهِ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ الْمُتَأَخِّرِينَ.
 وَعَامَّةُ مَا يُنْقَلُ عَنْ جُمْهُورِ الْعُلَمَاءِ أَنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَعْصُومِينَ عَنْ الْإِقْرَارِ عَلَى الصَّغَائِرِ وَلَا يُقَرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَلَا يَقُولُونَ إنَّهَا لَا تَقَعُ بِحَالِ وَأَوَّلُ مَنْ نُقِلَ عَنْهُمْ مِنْ طَوَائِفِ الْأُمَّةِ الْقَوْلُ بِالْعِصْمَةِ مُطْلَقًا وَأَعْظَمُهُمْ قَوْلًا لِذَلِكَ:
 الرَّافِضَةُ فَإِنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ بِالْعِصْمَةِ حَتَّى مَا يَقَعُ عَلَى سَبِيلِ النِّسْيَانِ وَالسَّهْوِ وَالتَّأْوِيلِ. وَيَنْقُلُونَ ذَلِكَ إلَى مَنْ يَعْتَقِدُونَ إمَامَتَهُ وَقَالُوا بِعِصْمَةِ عَلِيٍّ وَالِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ ثُمَّ 
" الْإِسْمَاعِيلِيَّة "
 الَّذِينَ كَانُوا مُلُوكَ الْقَاهِرَةِ وَكَانُوا يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ خُلَفَاءُ عَلَوِيُّونَ فَاطِمِيُّونَ وَهُمْ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ الْقَدَّاحِ كَانُوا هُمْ وَأَتْبَاعُهُمْ يَقُولُونَ بِمِثْلِ هَذِهِ الْعِصْمَةِ لِأَئِمَّتِهِمْ وَنَحْوِهِمْ مَعَ كَوْنِهِمْ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهِمْ أَبُو حَامِدٍ الْغَزَالِيُّ - فِي كِتَابِهِ الَّذِي صَنَّفَهُ فِي الرَّدِّ عَلَيْهِمْ -
 قَالَ:
 ظَاهِرُ مَذْهَبِهِمْ الرَّفْضُ وَبَاطِنُهُ الْكُفْرُ الْمَحْضُ. وَقَدْ صَنَّفَ 
" الْقَاضِي أَبُو يَعْلَى "
 وَصْفَ مَذَاهِبِهِمْ فِي كُتُبِهِ وَكَذَلِكَ غَيْرُ هَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَهَؤُلَاءِ وَأَمْثَالُهُمْ مِنْ الْغُلَاةِ الْقَائِلِينَ بِالْعِصْمَةِ وَقَدْ يُكَفِّرُونَ مَنْ يُنْكِرُ الْقَوْلَ بِهَا وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْغَالِيَةُ هُمْ كُفَّارٌ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَمَنْ كَفَّرَ الْقَائِلِينَ بِتَجْوِيزِ الصَّغَائِرِ عَلَيْهِمْ كَانَ مُضَاهِيًا لِهَؤُلَاءِ الْإِسْمَاعِيلِيَّة وَالْنُصَيْرِيَّة وَالرَّافِضَةِ وَالِاثْنَيْ عَشَرِيَّةَ. لَيْسَ هُوَ قَوْلَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَلَا مَالِكٍ وَلَا الشَّافِعِيِّ وَلَا الْمُتَكَلِّمِينَ - الْمُنْتَسِبِينَ إلَى السُّنَّةِ الْمَشْهُورِينَ - كَأَصْحَابِ
translated_text:
and in the early period, that view was reported only from the Rāfidīs, then from some Mu‘tazilīs, after which a group of later scholars agreed with them.

What is generally reported from the majority of scholars is that the prophets are not protected from being allowed to persist in minor sins, and that they are not allowed to persist in them. These scholars do not say that minor sins can never occur. Among the groups of this community, the first from whom unqualified protection from sin was reported, and its most emphatic proponents, were the Rāfidīs. They maintain that this protection extends even to matters arising from forgetfulness, inadvertence, or interpretation. They extend it to anyone they regard as an imam, and assert that ‘Alī and the Twelve are protected from sin.

Then the “Ismā‘īlīs,” who ruled Cairo and claimed to be caliphs descended from ‘Alī and Fātimah—though, according to the scholars, they were descendants of ‘Ubayd Allāh al-Qaddāh—and their followers asserted this same protection from sin for their imams and others like them. Yet they were as Abū Hāmid al-Ghazālī described them in the book he wrote to refute them:

“Outwardly, their doctrine is Rāfidism; inwardly, it is pure unbelief.”

“Al-Qādī Abū Ya‘lā” described their doctrines in his books, as did other Muslim scholars. These people and others like them are extremists who uphold protection from sin, and they may declare anyone who rejects it an unbeliever. These extremists are themselves unbelievers by the agreement of the Muslims. Thus, anyone who declares those who allow the possibility of prophets committing minor sins to be unbelievers resembles these Ismā‘īlīs, Nusayrīs, Rāfidīs, and Twelvers.

This is not the position of any of the followers of Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, or al-Shāfi‘ī, nor of the well-known speculative theologians who affiliate themselves with the Sunnah, such as the followers of

original_text: أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ كُلَّابٍ وَأَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إسْمَاعِيلَ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ كَرَّامٍ وَغَيْرِ هَؤُلَاءِ. وَلَا أَئِمَّةِ التَّفْسِيرِ وَلَا الْحَدِيثِ وَلَا التَّصَوُّفِ. لَيْسَ التَّكْفِيرُ بِهَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ قَوْلَ هَؤُلَاءِ فَالْمُكَفَّرُ بِمِثْلِ ذَلِكَ يُسْتَتَابُ فَإِنْ تَابَ وَإِلَّا عُوقِبَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ عُقُوبَةً تَرْدَعُهُ وَأَمْثَالَهُ عَنْ مِثْلِ هَذَا إلَّا أَنْ يَظْهَرَ مِنْهُ مَا يَقْتَضِي كُفْرَهُ وَزَنْدَقَتَهُ فَيَكُونُ حُكْمُهُ حُكْمَ أَمْثَالِهِ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْمُفَسَّقُ بِمِثْلِ هَذَا الْقَوْلِ يَجِبُ أَنْ يُعَزَّرَ بَعْدَ إقَامَةِ الْحُجَّةِ عَلَيْهِ؛ فَإِنَّ هَذَا تَفْسِيقٌ لِجُمْهُورِ أَئِمَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ. وَأَمَّا التَّصْوِيبُ وَالتَّخْطِئَةُ فِي ذَلِكَ فَهُوَ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْعُلَمَاءِ الْحَافِظِينَ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ الْمُنْتَسِبِينَ إلَى السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ. وَتَفْصِيلُ الْقَوْلِ فِي ذَلِكَ يَحْتَاجُ إلَى بَسْطٍ طَوِيلٍ لَا تَحْتَمِلُهُ هَذَا الْفَتْوَى. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ؟ .
translated_text:
Abū Muhammad ‘Abd Allāh ibn Sa‘īd ibn Kullāb, Abū al-Hasan ‘Alī ibn Ismā‘īl al-Ash‘arī, Abū ‘Abd Allāh Muhammad ibn Karrām, and others. Nor is it the position of the leading scholars of Quranic exegesis, hadith, or Sufism.

Declaring someone an unbeliever over this issue is not the position of these scholars. Anyone who makes such a declaration must therefore be called upon to repent. If he repents, well and good; otherwise, he must receive a punishment that deters him and others like him from doing such a thing—unless he manifests something that entails his own unbelief and heresy, in which case the ruling applicable to others of his kind applies to him.

Likewise, anyone who brands others as sinners for holding such a position must receive a discretionary punishment after the proof has been established against him, for this amounts to branding the majority of the leading scholars of Islam as sinners.

As for judging a position on this issue to be correct or mistaken, that is a matter discussed by well-versed Muslim scholars who adhere to the Sunnah and the community. A detailed treatment would require a lengthy exposition beyond the scope of this fatwa. And Allah knows best.

سُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى -:
عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ تَنَازَعَا فِي أَمْرِ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ 
" عِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ "
 - عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ -
 فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا:
 إنَّ عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ تَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ ثُمَّ رَفَعَهُ إلَيْهِ؛
 وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ:
 بَلْ رَفَعَهُ إلَيْهِ حَيًّا. فَمَا الصَّوَابُ فِي ذَلِكَ. وَهَلْ رَفَعَهُ بِجَسَدِهِ أَوْ رُوحِهِ أَمْ لَا؟ وَمَا الدَّلِيلُ عَلَى هَذَا وَهَذَا؟ وَمَا تَفْسِيرُ قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{إنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إلَيَّ}
 ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ،
 عِيسَى عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ حَيٌّ وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
" 
{يَنْزِلُ فِيكُمْ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ حَكَمًا عَدْلًا وَإِمَامًا مُقْسِطًا فَيَكْسِرُ الصَّلِيبَ وَيَقْتُلُ الْخِنْزِيرَ وَيَضَعُ الْجِزْيَةَ}
 "
 وَثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْهُ 
" 
{أَنَّهُ يَنْزِلُ عَلَى الْمَنَارَةِ الْبَيْضَاءِ شَرْقِيِّ دِمَشْقَ وَأَنَّهُ يَقْتُلُ الدَّجَّالَ}
 "
. وَمَنْ فَارَقَتْ رُوحُهُ جَسَدَهُ لَمْ يَنْزِلْ جَسَدُهُ مِنْ السَّمَاءِ وَإِذَا أُحْيِيَ فَإِنَّهُ يَقُومُ مِنْ قَبْرِهِ. وَأَمَّا قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{إنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ وَرَافِعُكَ إلَيَّ وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا}
 فَهَذَا دَلِيلٌ عَلَى أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَعْنِ بِذَلِكَ الْمَوْتَ؛ إذْ لَوْ أَرَادَ بِذَلِكَ الْمَوْتَ لَكَانَ عِيسَى فِي ذَلِكَ كَسَائِرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ؛ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَقْبِضُ أَرْوَاحَهُمْ وَيَعْرُجُ بِهَا إلَى السَّمَاءِ فَعُلِمَ أَنْ لَيْسَ فِي ذَلِكَ خَاصِّيَّةٌ.
 وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ:
 
{وَمُطَهِّرُكَ مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا}
 وَلَوْ
translated_text:
He—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked about two men who disagreed concerning Allah’s Prophet, “Jesus son of Mary”—peace be upon him. One said, “Allah caused Jesus son of Mary to die, then raised him to Himself.” The other said, “Rather, He raised him to Himself alive.” Which view is correct? Was he raised bodily or in spirit, or was he not raised? What is the evidence for each view? And what is the interpretation of the Most High’s words:

“I will take you and raise you to Myself”?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. Jesus—peace be upon him—is alive. It is established in an authentic hadith that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“The son of Mary will descend among you as a just judge and an equitable leader. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizyah tax.”

It is also established in an authentic hadith from him that:

“He will descend at the white minaret to the east of Damascus, and he will kill the Antichrist.”

When someone’s soul has departed from his body, his body does not descend from heaven. Rather, when he is brought back to life, he rises from his grave. As for the Most High’s words:

“I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you of those who disbelieve,”

this is evidence that He did not mean death by this. Had He meant death, Jesus would have been like all other believers in this respect: Allah takes their souls and raises them to heaven. Thus, it is clear that there would be nothing distinctive about this.

The same applies to His words:

“and purify you of those who disbelieve.”

And if

his soul had departed from his body, his body would have been in the earth, like the bodies of the rest of the prophets or of another prophet.

The Most High has said in another verse:

“They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them. Those who differ concerning him are indeed in doubt about him. They have no knowledge of him, but merely follow conjecture. They certainly did not kill him. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself.”

His words here, “Rather, Allah raised him to Himself,” make clear that He raised him in body and soul, just as it is established in authentic hadith that he will descend in body and soul. For had his death been intended, He would have said: “They did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; rather, he died.”

[His words, “Rather, Allah raised him to Himself,” make clear that He raised him in body and soul, just as it is established in authentic hadith that he will descend in body and soul] (*).

For this reason, some scholars explained “I will take you” as meaning, “I will take hold of you”—that is, “I will take your soul and body.” One says, “I have received the amount due in full,” using either tawaffaytu or istawfaytu. The word tawaffī (taking in full) does not, in itself, indicate taking the soul without the body, nor taking both together, except with a separate contextual indication.

It may also refer to the taking that occurs during sleep, as in the Most High’s words:

“Allah takes the souls at the time of their death.”

And His words:

“It is He who takes you by night and knows what you have done by day.”

And His words:

“Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him.”

They have discussed how the Messiah was taken, as set out in the relevant discussion elsewhere. And Allah Most High knows best.

translated_text:
The shaykh—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—was asked:

“Is it authentically reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that Allah, Blessed and Most High, brought his parents back to life for him, so that they embraced Islam through him and then died again?”

He replied:

No hadith scholar has authenticated this report. Rather, those versed in hadith unanimously agree that it is a lie and a fabrication. Although Abū Bakr—meaning al-Khatīb—transmitted a report to this effect in his book al-Sābiq wa-l-Lāhiq (Earlier and Later Transmitters), Abū al-Qāsim al-Suhaylī mentioned it in Sharh al-Sīra (Commentary on the Prophet’s Biography) with a chain of transmission containing unknown narrators, and Abū ‘Abd Allāh al-Qurtubī mentioned it in al-Tadhkira (The Reminder) and similar works, there is no disagreement among those versed in hadith that it is one of the most obvious fabrications, as scholars have explicitly stated.

It is not found in the authoritative hadith books: neither in the Sahīh collections, nor in the Sunan or Musnad collections, nor in other well-known hadith works. Nor have the authors of works on the Prophet’s military campaigns and Quranic exegesis mentioned it, even though they may transmit weak reports alongside authentic ones.

For its obvious falsehood cannot escape anyone committed to religion. Had such an event occurred, there would have been every incentive and reason to transmit it, for it would have been among the greatest departures from the ordinary course of events in two respects:

Al-Khatīb al-Baghdādī’s purpose in his book al-Sābiq wa-l-Lāhiq (Earlier and Later Transmitters) is to mention the earlier and later hadith transmitters who narrated from the same person, regardless of whether what they narrated was true or false. Ibn Shāhīn transmits good and bad material alike. Al-Suhaylī mentioned this report only with a chain containing unknown narrators. Moreover, it contradicts the Quran, the authentic Sunnah, and scholarly consensus.

Allah Most High says:

“Allah only accepts the repentance of those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon afterwards. It is those to whom Allah will turn in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.”

“But repentance is not for those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, ‘Indeed, I repent now,’ nor for those who die while they are disbelievers.”

Allah Most High thus makes clear that there is no repentance for one who dies as a disbeliever.

He Most High also says:

“But their faith did not benefit them once they saw Our punishment. That is Allah’s established way with His servants, and there the disbelievers lost.”

He thus declares that His established way with His servants is that faith does not benefit them once they have seen His punishment. How, then, could it benefit them after death? Other scriptural texts convey the same meaning.

In Sahīh Muslim, it is reported:

“A man said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ‘Where is my father?’ He replied, ‘Your father is in the Fire.’ When the man turned away, he called him back and said, ‘My father and your father are in the Fire.’”

and He granted me permission. I asked Him for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but He did not grant me permission. So visit graves, for they remind you of the Hereafter.”

In the hadith recorded in al-Musnad and elsewhere, he said:

“My mother is with your mother in the Fire.”

If it is said, “This occurred in the year of the conquest, whereas their revival took place afterwards, during the Farewell Pilgrimage”—which is why those who mentioned it did so, and which was the explanation offered by the author of al-Tadhkira (The Reminder)—this is false for several reasons:

First: Reports about what has happened or will happen are not subject to abrogation, such as His statement concerning Abū Lahab:

“He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame.”

And His statement concerning al-Walīd:

“I shall burden him with a steep ascent.”

The same applies to the statements, “My father and your father are in the Fire,” and, “My mother and your mother are in the Fire.” This is not a report about a Fire from which its inmates will emerge, as those guilty of major sins do. Had that been the case, seeking forgiveness for them would have been permissible. If Allah had known beforehand that they would believe, He would not have forbidden him to do so, for deeds are judged by their endings. Whoever dies as a believer will be forgiven by Allah, so seeking forgiveness for such a person would not be prohibited.

Second: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, visited his mother’s grave in the year of the conquest because it lay along his route, at al-Hajūn near Mecca. His father, however, was not there, and he did not visit him, since he was buried in Syria, away from his route. How, then, can it be claimed that his father was brought back to life for him?

Third: Had they both been believers whose faith benefited them, they would have been more deserving of renown and remembrance than his two uncles, Hamza and al-ʿAbbās. This is even more far-fetched than the claim made by the ignorant among the Rāfida and others like them

that Abū Tālib embraced faith. They cite the weak hadith in “al-Sīra” (The Prophetic Biography), which states that he uttered indistinct words at the time of his death. Had al-ʿAbbās stated that he had embraced faith, he would not have said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him:

“Your uncle, that misguided old man, used to help you. Have you done anything to benefit him?”

He replied:

“I found him deep in the Fire, so I interceded for him until he came to be in a shallow part of the Fire. On his feet are two sandals of fire that cause his brain to boil. Were it not for me, he would be in the lowest depth of the Fire.”

This claim is false and contradicts what is recorded in the Sahīh and elsewhere: the last thing he said was that he followed the religion of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, and al-ʿAbbās did not witness his death. Moreover, had that claim been true, Abū Tālib would have been more deserving of renown than Hamza and al-ʿAbbās. It is widely known throughout the Muslim community, through numerous reports handed down from earlier to later generations, that neither Abū Tālib nor the Prophet’s parents are mentioned among his believing family members, such as Hamza, al-ʿAbbās, ʿAlī, Fātima, al-Hasan and al-Husayn—may Allah be pleased with them. This is among the clearest proofs that the claim is a lie.

(Fourth: Allah Most High said, in the verse:

“You have had an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘We disavow you’”—up to His words—“‘I will certainly seek forgiveness for you, but I cannot avail you against Allah at all.’”

Allah Most High also said:

“Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him.”

The command, therefore, is to follow the example of Abraham and those with him, except in Abraham’s promise to seek forgiveness for his father. It is also stated that, when it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of Allah, he disowned him. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about these hadiths:

“The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Moses, peace be upon him, praying in his grave; he also saw him circumambulating the House and saw him in heaven. The same is reported of some other prophets. When someone dies, does he continue to perform deeds, even though the hadith states that his deeds come to an end? Does he benefit from this prayer and circumambulation? Did the Prophet see the prophets in these places in their bodies or in their souls?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. As for seeing Moses, peace be upon him, circumambulating the House, this was a dream, not something that occurred on the night of the Ascension. This is explicitly explained in the report; he likewise saw the Messiah and the False Messiah.

As for seeing Moses and the other prophets in heaven on the night of the Ascension—when he saw Adam in the lowest heaven, John and Jesus in the second, Joseph in the third, Idrīs in the fourth, Aaron in the fifth, Moses in the sixth, and Abraham in the seventh, or in the reverse order—he saw their souls taking the forms of their bodies.

Some have said that perhaps he saw the actual bodies buried in the graves. This view is without foundation.

translated_text:
But Jesus ascended to heaven in both soul and body, and the same has been said of Idrīs. Abraham, Moses, and the others, however, are buried in the earth. The Messiah—may Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him and all the other prophets—will certainly descend to earth at the white minaret east of Damascus. He will kill the False Messiah, break the cross, and kill swine, as established in authentic hadiths. This is why he was in the second heaven, although he is superior to Joseph, Idrīs, and Aaron: unlike the others, he intends to descend to earth before the Day of Resurrection.

Adam was in the lowest heaven because the souls of his descendants are presented to him: the souls of the blessed (whereas the gates of heaven will not be opened to the wretched, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle). He must therefore be close to them when they are presented to him.

As for the Prophet’s seeing Moses standing in prayer in his grave and also seeing him in heaven, there is no contradiction between the two. Souls are like angels in this respect: in a single instant, they ascend and descend as an angel does; they are not like the body in this regard. Elsewhere, I have discussed at length the states of souls after their separation from their bodies, mentioning some of the hadiths, transmitted reports, and evidence concerning this.

This prayer and similar acts bring enjoyment and delight to the deceased, just as the people of Paradise delight in glorifying Allah. They are inspired to glorify Him just as people in this world are inspired to breathe. This is not an act subject to religious responsibility for which a separate reward is sought; rather, the act itself is part of the bliss in which souls find enjoyment and delight.

The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“When a son of Adam dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which others benefit, and a righteous child who prays for him.”

By this, he meant deeds for which one receives a reward, not the acts in which one finds enjoyment. The people of Paradise delight in looking upon Allah, remembering Him, glorifying Him, and reciting the Quran. The reciter of the Quran will be told: “Recite and ascend, and recite with measured care as you used to recite in this world, for your station will be at the last verse you recite.”

They also delight in addressing their Lord and speaking intimately with Him. Although these things are deeds that earn a reward in this world, in the Hereafter they are acts that bring greater delight to the one performing them than eating, drinking, or sexual intercourse. These, too, are all acts. In this world, eating, drinking, and sexual intercourse are among the things one is enjoined to do and is rewarded for when accompanied by a righteous intention; in the Hereafter, they are themselves the reward in which one finds delight. And Allah knows best.

This is as much as this sheet could accommodate, for these matters call for lengthy discussion.
