translated_text:
The shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“Which of the sons of Abraham, Allah’s close friend—peace be upon him—was to be sacrificed: Ishmael or Isaac?”

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Scholars hold two well-known views on this question, each reported from a group of the early generations. Abū Ya‘lā mentioned two opinions transmitted from Ahmad on the matter and supported the view that it was Isaac, following Abū Bakr ‘Abd al-‘Azīz, who in turn followed Muhammad ibn Jarīr.

For this reason, Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī states that Ahmad’s followers support the view that it was Isaac. In fact, it is only these two and those who follow them who support it. This view is also attributed to Mālik himself, though a group of his followers disagreed with him.

Al-Sharīf Abū ‘Alī ibn Abī Mūsā stated that the correct position within Ahmad’s school is that it was Ishmael. This is what ‘Abd Allāh ibn Ahmad reported from his father, saying: “My father’s position was that it was Ishmael.”

In short, the disagreement over this question is well known. Nevertheless, what must be affirmed with certainty is that it was Ishmael. This is what the Quran, the Sunnah, and the well-known proofs establish. It is also what the Torah in the possession of the People of the Book indicates.

Moreover, it states that He said to Abraham:

“Sacrifice your son, your only son.”

In another translation: “Your firstborn.” Ishmael was his only son and his firstborn, as Muslims and the People of the Book agree. However, the People of the Book altered the text by adding Isaac’s name. Those who took this from them transmitted it, and the belief that it was Isaac spread among some Muslims. Its origin lies in the textual distortion by the People of the Book.

Further evidence that it was Ishmael is the account of the son to be sacrificed in Surah al-Sāffāt. Allah Most High says:

“So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy.”

These good tidings contained three assurances: that the child would be a boy, that he would reach puberty, and that he would be forbearing. What forbearance could be greater than his when his father told him of the sacrifice and he replied:

“You will find me, if Allah wills, among the steadfast”?

It has been said that no quality is used less frequently by Allah to describe the prophets than forbearance, because it is so rarely found. He did describe Abraham with it in His words:

“Indeed, Abraham was tender-hearted and forbearing.”

“Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, tender-hearted, and ever turning to Allah.”

For this event attested to the forbearance of them both:

“When he was old enough to work alongside him, he said, ‘My son, I have seen in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so consider what you think.’ He replied, ‘My father, do as you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the steadfast.’”

—up to His words—

“And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.”

“And We left this tribute to him among later generations.”

“Peace be upon Abraham.”

“Thus do We reward those who do good.”

“Indeed, he was one of Our believing servants.”

“And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet among the righteous.”

“And We blessed him and Isaac. Among their descendants are those who do good and those who clearly wrong themselves.”

This account indicates that it was Ishmael in several ways:

- (First: He gave him good tidings of the son to be sacrificed and related his story first. Once He had completed that account, He said:

“And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet among the righteous.”

“And We blessed him and Isaac.”

He thus made clear that these were two announcements: good tidings of the son to be sacrificed, and a second announcement concerning Isaac. This is plain.

(Second: He relates the account of the son to be sacrificed nowhere else in the Quran. In the other passages, He mentions only the good tidings of Isaac, as in Surah Hūd, where He Most High says:

“And his wife was standing, and she laughed. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.”

Had Isaac been the son to be sacrificed, this would have contradicted the promise concerning Jacob.

He Most High also says:

“He felt afraid of them. They said, ‘Do not fear,’ and gave him good tidings of a learned boy.”

“Then his wife came forward with a cry, struck her face, and said, ‘A barren old woman!’”

He Most High says in Surah al-Hijr:

“They said, ‘Do not be afraid. We bring you good tidings of a learned boy.’”

“He said, ‘Do you bring me good tidings when old age has overtaken me? What good tidings, then, do you bring?’”

“They said, ‘We bring you good tidings in truth, so do not be among those who despair.’”

He did not mention that this was the son to be sacrificed. Then, when He mentioned both announcements together—the good tidings of the son to be sacrificed, followed by the good tidings of Isaac—this provided evidence that Isaac was not the son to be sacrificed. This is further supported by His mention of His gift of Isaac and Jacob to Abraham—may Allah have mercy on him—in His words:

“And We granted him Isaac, and Jacob as an additional gift, and made each of them righteous.”

And His words:

“And We granted him Isaac and Jacob, and placed prophethood and Scripture among his descendants. We gave him his reward in this world, and in the Hereafter he will surely be among the righteous.”

Allah did not mention the son to be sacrificed.

The third point: He described the son to be sacrificed as a forbearing boy, whereas elsewhere, when mentioning the good tidings of Isaac, He spoke of a learned boy. There must be wisdom in this distinction,

and this further supports the association of the two qualities. Forbearance is suited to patience, which was the character of the son to be sacrificed. Ishmael is described as patient in His words, Most High:

“And Ishmael, Idrīs, and Dhū al-Kifl—all were among the patient.”

This, too, is a third point, for He relates that the son to be sacrificed said:

“O my father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.”

Allah described Ishmael as being among the patient. Allah Most High also described Ishmael as true to his promise in His words:

“Indeed, he was true to his promise.”

This is because he promised his father that he would patiently endure being sacrificed, and he fulfilled that promise.

The fourth point:

The good tidings of Isaac were miraculous, because the elderly woman was barren. Thus Allah’s intimate friend—peace be upon him—said:

“Do you bring me good tidings when old age has overtaken me? What good tidings, then, do you bring?”

His wife said:

“Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman and this husband of mine is an old man?”

It has already been explained that the good tidings of Isaac came in old age, and that they were given to both Abraham and his wife.

The good tidings of the son to be sacrificed, however, were given to Abraham—peace be upon him—and it was he, rather than the mother who had been given good tidings of the child, who was tested by being commanded to sacrifice him. This accords with what is transmitted from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and his Companions in the Sahīh and elsewhere: when Hagar gave birth to Ishmael, Sarah became jealous, so Abraham went

How, then, could He command that Isaac be sacrificed after that? The good tidings of Jacob entail that Isaac would live and that Jacob would be born to him. There is no disagreement among people that the incident of the intended sacrifice took place before Jacob’s birth. Another indication of this is that the incident of the intended sacrifice took place in Mecca:

“When the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—conquered Mecca, the ram’s two horns were in the Kaaba. For this reason, Minā was made a site for religious rites from the time of Abraham and Ishmael—peace be upon them both—and, as the Quran explicitly states, it was they who built the House. No one, whether from the People of the Book or anyone else, has reported that Isaac went to Mecca. He was also asked—may Allah have mercy on him—about al-Khidr and Elijah: “Have their lives been prolonged? Explain this to us, may Allah Most High have mercy on you.”

He replied:

Ibrāhīm al-Harbī asked Ahmad ibn Hanbal about the prolonged lives of al-Khidr and Elijah, and the claim that they remain alive, see, and have reports transmitted from them. Imam Ahmad said: “Whoever refers to an absent person has not acted fairly; only a devil put this idea forward.”

Al-Bukhārī was asked about al-Khidr and Elijah: “Are they among the living?” He replied: “How could that be, when the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘At the end of a hundred years, none of those now on the face of the earth will remain’?”

“We did not grant immortality to any human before you.”

The quotation from Ibn al-Jawzī at the end of this fatwa is defective, as the context indicates—and Allah knows best. It appears that some text has been omitted here.

Ibn al-Jawzī, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote a book on this subject entitled Ujālat al-Muntazir fī Sharh Hāl al-Khidr (A Brief Explanation of al-Khidr’s State for the Awaiting Reader). Ibn Kathīr, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned it in his history (2:265), saying:

“As for those who held that he had died, they include al-Bukhārī, Ibrāhīm al-Harbī, Abū al-Husayn ibn al-Munādī, and Shaykh Abū al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzī, who defended this position and wrote a book entitled Ujālat al-Muntazir fī Sharh Hāl al-Khidr. Many arguments may be advanced in support of their position, including Allah Most High’s statement: ‘We did not grant immortality to any human before you.’ Thus, if al-Khidr is human, he necessarily falls within this general statement. The presumption is that no exception exists until one is established. No evidence establishing an exception has been cited from an authority protected from error whose report must be accepted.”

Thus, perhaps Ibn al-Jawzī’s concluding comments on the verse, or something similar, are what has been omitted from the fatwa. Allah Most High knows best.

translated_text:
The shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

“Was al-Khidr, peace be upon him, a prophet or a friend of Allah? Is he still alive? If he is alive, what do you say about the saying attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

‘If he were alive, he would have visited me.’

Is this hadith authentic or not?”

He replied:

As for his prophethood, after the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, neither he nor any other person received revelation. As for the period before the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was sent, there is disagreement over whether al-Khidr was a prophet (*).

Those who say that he was a prophet do not say that he was stripped of prophethood. Rather, they say that, like Elijah, he is a prophet, but that he has received no revelation during these times. The withholding of revelation from him for a particular period does not negate his actual prophethood, just as revelation might be interrupted for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, during his prophetic mission.

Most scholars hold that he was not a prophet, although much of the prophethood among those before us closely resembles the divinely bestowed gifts and perfection found within this community. Nevertheless, every one of the prophets is superior to every

(*) Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd said (pp. 35–37):
The compiler—may Allah have mercy on him—expressed doubt about this fatwa (the compiler meant here is Abd al-Rahmān ibn al-Qāsim), commenting at its beginning: “This is how I found this treatise.” It appears that it is not by the shaykh, since it contradicts his statements elsewhere that al-Khidr has died:

1 - One such statement appears one page before this fatwa. When asked whether al-Khidr and Elijah were alive, he replied: “Neither is among the living, nor have they been granted prolonged lifespans.”

2 - Another is his statement in al-Fatāwā, 1:249: “Al-Khidr who accompanied Moses has died, as explained elsewhere.”

3 - Another is his statement in al-Minhāj, 4:93: “All the scholars who have critically examined the matter hold that he has died.”

4 - Another is his statement in al-Fatāwā, 27:100–101: “The correct view, held by scholars who have critically examined the matter, is that he is dead and did not live to see the advent of Islam. Had he been alive in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, he would have been obliged to believe in him and strive alongside him, as Allah required of him and others. He would have been in Mecca and Medina. It would have been more fitting for him to join the Companions in striving alongside them and supporting them in the religion than to visit some unbelievers to patch their ship. Nor would he have concealed himself from the best community brought forth for humankind…” He went on to say: “If al-Khidr remains perpetually alive, how is it that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, never mentioned this or informed his community of it, nor did his rightly guided caliphs?!”

5 - Another is what Ibn Abd al-Hādī, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in al-Uqūd al-Durriyya while discussing the shaykh’s writings (p. 70): “A response concerning al-Khidr: whether he has died or is alive. He adopted the view that he has died.”

one of those foremost in truthfulness, as the Quran ranks them, and as it is reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The sun has neither risen nor set upon anyone superior to Abu Bakr al-Siddīq, apart from the prophets and messengers.”

It is also reported that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“A man would indeed hear the sound and thereby be a prophet.”

Within this community, however, there are people who hear it and see the light without being prophets. Whatever such a person sees and hears must be assessed against what Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, brought. If it agrees with that, it is true. If it contradicts it, he knows with certainty that what has come from Allah is sure knowledge, untainted by doubt, and needs no corroboration through agreement with anything else.

As for whether al-Khidr is alive: he is alive. The hadith mentioned has no basis, and no chain of transmission is known for it. Rather, what is reported in Musnad al-Shāfi‘ī and elsewhere is that he met the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Anyone who says that he did not meet the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has spoken without knowledge, for this is a matter that cannot be known exhaustively.

Whoever argues that he has died on the basis of the Prophet’s statement, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred years, none of those who are on the face of the earth today will remain upon it.”

This provides no proof, for it is possible that al-Khidr was on the face of the earth at that time. Furthermore, the correct view is that the Dajjāl—and likewise al-Jassāsah—was alive and in existence

Whatever answer is given concerning him also applies to al-Khidr: namely, that the word “earth” may not have been included in this report, or that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, may have meant ordinary, known human beings. Those whose circumstances depart from the ordinary would then fall outside its general scope, just as the jinn do, even if the wording encompasses both jinn and human beings. Exceptions of this kind to such general wording are frequent and customary. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He was also asked:

“Does the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, know the time of the Hour?”

He replied:

As for the report in question—that he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, “knows the time of the Hour”—it has no basis. There is no statement whatsoever from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, specifying the time of the Hour. Rather, Allah Most High has said:

“They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place? Say, ‘Knowledge of it rests only with my Lord. None but He will reveal it at its appointed time.’ It weighs heavily upon the heavens and the earth.”

That is, its time is hidden from the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth. Allah Most High also said to Moses:

“Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it.”

Ibn ‘Abbās and others said: “I almost conceal it from Myself; how, then, could it be made known?”

In the two Sahīh collections, on the authority of Abū Hurayrah, and also in Muslim’s Sahīh, on the authority of ‘Umar, it is reported:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was asked, ‘When is the Hour?’ He replied, ‘The one being questioned about it knows no more than the questioner.’”

Thus, he stated that he knew no more about it than the questioner. The questioner appeared in the form of a Bedouin, and he did not know that it was Gabriel until after he had departed. When he answered him, he thought he was simply a Bedouin. So if the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said of himself that he knew no more about the Hour than

As for those who have spoken about its precise time—such as the man who wrote a book entitled “Al-Durr al-munazzam fī ma‘rifat al-a‘zam” (The Ordered Pearl on Knowledge of the Greatest), mentioning ten indications by which he specified its time; those who discussed this on the basis of the letters of the alphabet; the one who discussed it in “‘Anqā’ mughrib”; and others like them—although they may enjoy an exalted standing among their followers, most of them are liars and fabricators. translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām was asked:
“Who is superior: the righteous among the children of Adam or the angels?”

He replied that righteous human beings are superior in terms of their ultimate perfection, whereas the angels are superior in terms of their initial state. The angels are now in the highest company, free from what besets the children of Adam and wholly absorbed in worshipping the Lord. There is no doubt that their present state is more perfect than that of human beings. On the Day of Resurrection, however, after entering Paradise, righteous human beings will attain a more perfect state than that of the angels.

Ibn al-Qayyim said:
“This distinction makes clear the underlying basis of superiority, reconciles the evidence of both sides, and brings them into agreement while acknowledging the truth held by each (*).”

translated_text:
He was also asked:
“Are the obedient among the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, superior to the angels?”

He replied:
It is established that ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr said:

“The angels said, ‘Our Lord, You have allowed the children of Adam to eat, drink and enjoy themselves in this world, so grant us the Hereafter as You have granted them this world.’ He said, ‘I will not do so.’ They repeated their request to Him, and He said, ‘I will not do so.’ Then they repeated their request to Him twice or three times, and He said, ‘By My might, I will not make the righteous descendants of the one whom I created with My two hands like those to whom I said, “Be,” and they came into being.’”

ʿUthmān ibn Saʿīd al-Dārimī mentioned this report, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ahmad narrated it in his book al-Sunan (*) as a report attributed to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with a disconnected chain of transmission.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām also said:
“Allah has created no being more honoured in His sight than Muhammad.” He was asked, “Not even Gabriel or Michael?” He replied to the questioner, “Do you know what Gabriel and Michael are? Gabriel and Michael are but created beings subject to His command, like the sun and the moon. Allah has created no being more honoured in His sight than Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

I know of nothing reported from any of the Companions that contradicts this. This is the well-known position among those who affiliate themselves with the Sunnah, including the followers of the four imams and others: that the prophets and the friends of Allah are superior to the angels. We have devoted a separate work to this question, in which we presented the evidence on both sides.

translated_text:
The shaykh—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked about Adam:

“When Allah created him, breathed into him of His spirit, and made His angels prostrate to him, did the angels of heaven and earth prostrate, or only the angels of earth? Were Gabriel and Michael among those who prostrated? Was the garden in which he dwelt the Paradise of Eternity, which already exists, or a garden on earth that Allah created for him? When he was sent down, was he sent down from heaven to earth, or from one land to another, as with the Children of Israel?”

He replied:

All praise is due to Allah. Rather, He made all the angels prostrate to him, as the Quran expressly states in His words, exalted is He:

“So the angels prostrated, all of them together.”

These are three expressions affirming universality and exhaustive inclusion. His words “the angels” encompass all the angels, for a collective noun made definite by the definite article denotes universality. Thus, in His words, “Lord of the angels and the Spirit,” He is the Lord of all the angels.

The second expression is “all of them,” which is among the strongest expressions of universality.

The third is His word “together,” which reinforces that universality. Whoever says that not all the angels prostrated to him, but only the angels of earth, has rejected the Quran

translated_text:
with lies and slander. This view and others like it are not the views of Muslims, Jews, or Christians. Rather, they are the views of heretical adherents of philosophy who identify “angels” with the soul’s good faculties and “devils” with its evil faculties. They interpret the angels’ prostration as the faculties’ obedience to reason, and the devils’ refusal as the evil faculties’ disobedience to reason. Such notions are advanced by the authors of the “Epistles of the Brethren of Purity” and others like them among the Qarmatian esotericists, as well as misguided speculative theologians and devotees who follow their path. Similar views may also be found among statements attributed to Quran commentators without any reliable chain of transmission.

The position of Muslims, Jews, and Christians is what Allah has related in the Quran. None of the devils were among those commanded to prostrate; their father, Iblīs, however, was commanded to do so, but refused and disobeyed. Some people counted him among the angels because he was included in the command to prostrate. Others counted him among the jinn because he has a tribe and offspring, and because he was created from fire, whereas the angels were created from light.

The correct understanding is that he was one of them in respect of his form, but not in respect of his origin or his likeness. Not one of the angels failed to prostrate to Adam: neither Gabriel nor Michael nor anyone else. As for the contrary views mentioned by the author of Khawāss al-Qur’ān and others like him, their statements are false. We have explained their unsoundness and falsity in an extensive discussion for which this is not the place. This is among the proofs cited by Ahl al-Sunnah that Adam and others among the prophets and allies of Allah

are superior to all the angels, because Allah commanded the angels to prostrate before Adam in his honour. Thus Iblīs said:

“Do You see this one whom You have honoured above me?”

This indicates that Adam was honoured above those who prostrated before him.

According to the early generations of the Muslim community and Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamā‘ah, the “Paradise” in which Allah settled Adam and his wife is the everlasting Paradise. Whoever says that it was a garden on earth, in India, Jeddah, or elsewhere, belongs to the adherents of philosophy and the heretics, or to their fellows among the speculative theologians who introduce religious innovations. This view is held by some adherents of philosophy and some Mu‘tazilites. The Quran and the Sunnah refute it, and the early generations of the Muslim community and its leading scholars agree that it is false.

Allah Most High said:

“And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate before Adam,’ they prostrated, except Iblīs. He refused and was arrogant, and was among the disbelievers.”

“And We said, ‘O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise,’”

up to His words:

“And We said, ‘Descend, as enemies to one another. On earth you will have a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time.’”

He thus tells us that He, glorified be He, commanded them to descend, and that they were enemies to one another. He then said:

“On earth you will have a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time.”

This shows that they were not on earth, but were made to descend to it. Had they been on earth and moved to another land—as the people of Moses moved from one land to another—their place of settlement and enjoyment for a time would have been on earth both before and after their descent. Likewise, in Sūrat al-A‘rāf, when Iblīs said:

“I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay,”

Allah said:

“Then descend from it! It is not for you to be arrogant there.”

Thus His words:

“Then descend from it! It is not for you to be arrogant there.”

show that heaven and Paradise are singled out for this ruling. The pronoun in His words “from it” refers to something known, though not explicitly mentioned. This differs from His words:

“Go down to a town, and you will have what you have asked for.”

For there He did not mention the place in which they were made to descend, and here He said, “Descend,” because descent is from a higher place to a lower one. The Children of Israel were near the land of al-Sarāh, facing al-Sarāh, which overlooked the town to which they were descending. Someone who goes down from a mountain into a valley is said to have descended.

(Furthermore, the Children of Israel were travelling from place to place. When a traveller reaches a town, he is said to have “alighted there,” because he ordinarily rides during his journey and dismounts from his animals upon arrival. Thus one says, “The army alighted in such-and-such a land,” or “The caravan alighted in such-and-such a land,” because they dismounted from their animals. The word for alighting is like the word for descending: “descended” is used only for movement from a higher place to a lower one.

And His words in the two verses:

“Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.”

“He said, ‘Descend.’”

His statement here, following His words:

“Descend, as enemies to one another. On earth you will have a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time.”

makes clear that they descended to the earth from somewhere other than it. And His words:

“There you will live, there you will die, and from there you will be brought forth.”

are evidence that, before this, they were not in a place where they would live, die, and be brought forth. They came to that place only when they were made to descend from Paradise.

 فَلِمَاذَا تَلُومُنِي عَلَى أَمْرٍ قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُخْلَقَ؟
 فَقَالَ:
 فَحَجَّ آدَمَ مُوسَى}
 "
 وَمُوسَى إنَّمَا لَامَ آدَمَ لِمَا حَصَلَ لَهُ وَذُرِّيَّتُهُ بِالْخُرُوجِ مِنْ الْجَنَّةِ مِنْ الْمَشَقَّةِ وَالنَّكَدِ فَلَوْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ بُسْتَانًا فِي الْأَرْضِ لَكَانَ غَيْرُهُ مِنْ بَسَاتِينِ الْأَرْضِ يُعَوِّضُ عَنْهُ. (وَآدَمُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ احْتَجَّ بِالْقَدَرِ؛ لِأَنَّ الْعَبْدَ مَأْمُورٌ عَلَى أَنْ يَصْبِرَ عَلَى مَا قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ مِنْ الْمَصَائِبِ وَيَتُوبَ إلَيْهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرَهُ مِنْ الذُّنُوبِ والمعائب. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
There are many scriptural texts to this effect, as well as statements by the early generations and the imams.

In the two Sahīh collections, Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, reports that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said:

“Adam and Moses debated. Moses said, ‘Adam, you are the father of mankind. Allah created you with His Hand, breathed into you of His spirit, and made His angels prostrate before you. Why, then, did you cause us and your descendants to leave Paradise?’

Adam replied, ‘You are Moses, whom Allah chose to bear His message and to whom He spoke. Do you find in the Torah: “Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray”?’

He said, ‘Yes.’

Adam said, ‘Why, then, do you blame me for something Allah decreed for me before I was created?’”

The Prophet said, “Thus Adam prevailed over Moses in the argument.”

Moses blamed Adam only for the hardship and misery that befell him and his descendants through leaving Paradise. Had it merely been a garden on earth, another earthly garden could have replaced it.

(Adam, peace be upon him, appealed to divine decree because a servant is commanded to bear patiently the calamities Allah has decreed, and to repent to Him and seek His forgiveness for sins and faults. And Allah knows best.

original_text:
قَالَ شَيْخُ الْإِسْلَامِ:
فَصْلٌ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ الْمَشْهُورَةِ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ فِي 
" التَّفْضِيلِ بَيْنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ "
قَالَ:
 الْكَلَامُ إمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي التَّفْضِيلِ بَيْنَ الْجِنْسِ: الْمَلَكِ وَالْبَشَرِ؛ أَوْ بَيْنَ صَالِحِي الْمَلَكِ وَالْبَشَرِ.
 أَمَّا الْأَوَّلُ وَهُوَ أَنْ يُقَالَ:
 أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ: الْمَلَائِكَةُ أَوْ الْبَشَرُ؟
 فَهَذِهِ كَلِمَةٌ تَحْتَمِلُ أَرْبَعَةَ أَنْوَاعٍ:
 
(*)
النَّوْعُ الْأَوَّلُ أَنْ يُقَالَ:
 هَلْ كَلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ آحَادِ النَّاسِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ كُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ آحَادِ الْمَلَائِكَةِ؟
 فَهَذَا لَا يَقُولُهُ عَاقِلٌ فَإِنَّ فِي النَّاسِ:
 الْكُفَّارَ وَالْفُجَّارَ وَالْجَاهِلِينَ والمستكبرين وَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَفِيهِمْ مَنْ هُوَ مِثْلُ الْبَهَائِمِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ السَّائِمَةِ بَلْ الْأَنْعَامُ أَحْسَنُ حَالًا مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ كَمَا نَطَقَ بِذَلِكَ الْقُرْآنُ فِي مَوَاضِعَ مِثْلِ قَوْله تَعَالَى. 
{إنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ الْبُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ}
 وَقَالَ
translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām said:

Chapter on the well-known question of “The Relative Merit of Angels and Humans”

He said:

The discussion may concern either the relative merit of angels and humans as two kinds of beings, or the relative merit of the righteous among angels and humans.

As for the first question—“Which are superior: angels or humans?”—it admits of four interpretations:

(*)
The first interpretation is to ask: Is every individual human superior to every individual angel?

No rational person would say this. Among humans are disbelievers, the wicked, the ignorant, the arrogant, and believers. Among them are those who resemble beasts and grazing livestock. Indeed, livestock are better off than these people, as the Quran explicitly states in several places, such as His saying, exalted is He:

“Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason.”

And He said:

original_text:
تَعَالَى:
 
{إنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ}
 وَقَالَ: 
{وَلَقَدْ ذَرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا وَلَهُمْ آذَانٌ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا أُولَئِكَ كَالْأَنْعَامِ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْغَافِلُونَ}
 وَالدَّوَابُّ جَمْعُ دَابَّةٍ وَهُوَ كُلُّ مَا دَبَّ فِي سَمَاءٍ وَأَرْضٍ مِنْ إنْسٍ وَجِنٍّ وَمَلَكٍ وَبَهِيمَةٍ فَفِي الْقُرْآنِ مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى تَفْضِيلِ الْبَهَائِمِ عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِنْ النَّاسِ فِي خَمْسِ آيَاتٍ. وَقَدْ وَضَعَ 
" ابْنُ الْمَرْزُبَانِ "
 كِتَابَ (تَفْضِيلُ الْكِلَابِ عَلَى كَثِيرٍ مِمَّنْ لَبِسَ الثِّيَابَ وَقَدْ جَاءَ فِي ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْمَأْثُورِ مَا لَا نَسْتَطِيعُ إحْصَاءَهُ مِثْلُ مَا فِي مُسْنَدِ أَحْمَدَ: 
{رُبَّ مَرْكُوبَةٍ أَكْثَرُ ذِكْرًا مِنْ رَاكِبِهَا}
 ".
 وَفَضْلُ الْبَهَائِمِ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ وُجُوهٍ:
 أَحَدُهَا: أَنَّ الْبَهِيمَةَ لَا سَبِيلَ لَهَا إلَى كَمَالٍ وَصَلَاحٍ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا تَصْنَعُهُ وَالْإِنْسَانُ لَهُ سَبِيلٌ لِذَلِكَ فَإِذَا لَمْ يَبْلُغْ صَلَاحَهُ وَكَمَالَهُ الَّذِي خُلِقَ لَهُ بَانَ نَقْصُهُ وَخُسْرَانُهُ مِنْ هَذَا الْوَجْهِ.
 وَثَانِيهَا:
 أَنَّ الْبَهَائِمَ لَهَا أَهْوَاءٌ وَشَهَوَاتٌ: بِحَسَبِ إحْسَاسِهَا وَشُعُورِهَا وَلَمْ تُؤْتَ تَمْيِيزًا وَفُرْقَانًا بَيْنَ مَا يَنْفَعُهَا وَيَضُرُّهَا وَالْإِنْسَانُ قَدْ أُوتِيَ ذَلِكَ.
 وَهَذَا الَّذِي يُقَالُ:
 الْمَلَائِكَةُ لَهُمْ عُقُولٌ بِلَا شَهَوَاتٍ وَالْبَهَائِمُ لَهَا شَهَوَاتٌ بِلَا عُقُولٍ وَالْإِنْسَانُ لَهُ شَهَوَاتٌ وَعَقْلٌ. فَمَنْ غَلَبَ عَقْلُهُ شَهْوَتَهُ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ الْمَلَائِكَةِ أَوْ مِثْلُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ وَمَنْ غَلَبَتْ شَهْوَتُهُ عَقْلَهُ فَالْبَهَائِمُ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ.
original_footnote:
قال الشيخ ناصر بن حمد الفهد (ص ٣٨ - ٤٣):
وأريد أن أنبه إلى أمرين:
الأمر الأول: أن هذه الرسالة أشك في نسبتها لشيخ الإسلام رحمه الله، فمن قرأ للشيخ وعرف نَفَسَهُ في رسائله وفتاواه سيعرف هذا جيدا، فإما أن يكون أصلها للشيخ رحمه الله وخلط كلامه بكلام غيره ولم يميز بين الكلامين، أو أنها لأحد تلاميذه المتأثرين به، ونحو ذلك، أما أن تكون جميع هذه الرسالة للشيخ فهو مما أستبعده والله أعلم، فالطريقة التي كتبت بها هذه الرسالة مغايرة لطريقة الشيخ في الجملة، وسأذكر هنا بعض الأمثلة على ذلك:
١ - ص ٣٥٩ (هذا هو العجب العجيب).
٢ - ص ٣٦٤ (فافهم هذا فإن تحته سر)
٣ - ص ٣٦٥، ٣٦٦ (فافهم هذا فإنه مجلاة شبهة ومصفاة كدر).
٤ - ص ٣٦٦ (والله أكبر كبيرا)
٥ - ص ٣٧٤، ٣٧٥ (فلا تلجَنَّ باب إنكار، ورد وإمساك وإغماض ردا لظاهره وتعجبًا من باطنه حفظًا لقواعدك التي كتبتها بقواك وضبطتها بأصولك التي عقلتك عن جَنَاب مولاك، إياك مما يخالف المتقدمين من التنزيه وتَوَقّ التمثيل والتشبيه، ولعمري إن هذا هو الصراط المستقيم، الذي هو أَحَدَّ من السيف، وأدق من الشعر، ومن لم يجعل الله له نورًا فما له من نور).
٦ - ص ٣٥٢ (لا علم لي بحقيقته) وص ٣٥٣ (هذا غير معلوم والله أعلم بخلقه)، وص ٣٥٤ (لكن الذي سنح لي والله أعلم بالصواب)، وص ٣٦١ (ولعل ذلك والله أعلم بحقائق الأمور)، ص ٣٦٤ (ولا حاجة بنا إلى تفسير كلام ربنا بآرائنا والله أعلم بتفسيره).
٧ - ص ٣٧٤ (وهذا بحر يغرق فيه السابح، لا يخوضه إلا كل مؤيد بنور الهداية، وإلا وقع إما في تمثيل، أو في تعطيل. فليكن ذو اللب على بصيرة أن وراء علمه مرماة بعيدة، وفوق كل ذي علم عليم)
٨ - ص ٣٧٥ (ولو ثبت أن علم البشر في الدنيا لا يكون إلا على أيدى الملائكة وهو والله باطل).
٩ - ص ٣٧٩ (فهذا هداك الله وجه التفضيل بالأسباب المعلومة، ذكرنا منه أنموذجًا) وص ٣٨١ (فاعلم - نو الله قلبك وشرح صدرك للإسلام -).
ثانيا: وصف المخالفين له بما لم يعهد عنه، نحو:
١ - ص ٣٥٨ (وقد قال بعض الأغبياء: إن السجود إنما كان لله وجعل آدم قبلة لهم).
٢ - ص ٣٦٢ (فاعلم أن المقالة أولا ليس معها ما يوجب قبولها، لا مسموع، ولا معقول، إلا خواطر، وسوانح، ووساوس، مادتها من عرش إبليس).
٣ - ص ٣٦٣ (ومن اختلج في سره وجه الخصوص بعد هذا التحقيق والتوكيل فليعز نفسه في الاستدلال بالقرآن والفهم، فإنه لا يثق بشئ يؤخذ منه، ياليت شعري! لو كانت الملائكة كلهم سجدوا وأراد الله أن يخبرنا بذلك، فأي كلمة أتم وأعم، أم يأتي قول يقال: أليس هذا من أبين البيان؟)
٤ - ص ٣٧٦ (وليس كما زعم هذا الغبي).
٥ - ص ٣٩١ (وهذا من أوضح الكلام لمن له فقه بالعربية ونعوذ بالله من التنطع).
ثالثا: قوله ص ٣٧٩ في معرض تفضيله صالحي البشر على الملائكة (وأين هم عن الذين: {وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلَى أَنفُسِهِمْ وَلَوْ كَانَ بِهِمْ خَصَاصَةٌ}؟ وأين هم ممن يدعون إلى الهدى ودين الحق؛ ومن سَنَّ سُنَّة حسنة؟ وأين هم من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (إن من أمتي من يشفع في أكثر من ربيعة ومُضَر)؟ وأين هم من الأقطاب، والأوتاد، والأغواث، والأبدال، والنجباء؟).
وقد علق الجامع على رحمه الله على الجملة الأخيرة بقوله (هكذا بالأصل)، وهذا يدل على أنه استنكر مثل هذه العبارة، والشيخ رحمه الله له كلام على إبطال هذه الأسماء وأنها لم ترد في الكتاب ولا في السنة، ومن ذلك:
قوله في الفتاوى ١١/ ٤٣٣ (أما الأسماء الدائرة على ألسنة كثير من النساك والعامة مثل الغوث الذي بمكة،
والأوتاد الأربعة والأقطاب السبعة والأبدال الأربعين والنجباء الثلاثمائة: فهذه أسماء ليست موجودة في كتاب الله تعالى؛ ولا هي أيضًا مأثورة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإسناد صحيح، ولا ضعيف. . . الخ الفتوى وهي طويلة مفصلة).
وقال في (المنهاج) ١/ ٩٣ (وأيضا فجميع هذه الألفاظ لفظ الغوث والقطب والأوتاد والنجباء وغيرها لم ينقل أحد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإسناد معروف أنه تكلم بشيء منها ولا أصحابه ولكن لفظ الأبدال تكلم به بعض السلف ويروى فيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حديث ضعيف).
وفي الجملة: فهذه الرسالة نفسها ليس نفس شيخ الإسلام رحمه الله في رسائله، والله أعلم.
الأمر الثاني: أنه حصل تصحيفات يسيرة في هذه الرسالة، ومن ذلك:
١ - ص ٣٥٣ (وكان في نوع المفضول ما هو خير من كثير من أعيان النوع الفاضل؛ كالحمار والفأرة والفرس الزمن، والمرأة الصالحة مع الرجل الفاجر)
قلت: (كالحمار والفأرة) صوابه: (كالحمار الفاره)
٢ - ص ٣٥٧ (وروى عبد الله في (التفسير))، وذكر هذا الأثر سابقا ص ٢٤٤ وقال فيه (عبد الله في (السنن)) وجاء في ص ٣٦٩ (السنة) وهو الأظهر، والله أعلم.
٣ - ص ٣٦٠ (والبهائم لا تعبد الله)، ولعله: لا تعبد إلا الله.
٤ - ص ٣٦٤ (وإذا كانت القصة قد تكررت وليس فيها ما يدل على الخصوص فليس دعوى الخصوص فيها من البهتان).
قلت: ويظهر أن العبارة: (كان دعوى الخصوص فيها من البهتان) أو (فإن دعوى الخصوص)، ونحو ذلك.
٥ - ص ٣٦٨: ذكر الدليل الثامن، ثم في السطر الثاني عشر قال: (ثم ذكر ما رواه الخلال. . .)، وهذا يجل على أمرين:
الأول: حصول اختصار، لأن (الدليل التاسع) و (العاشر) لم تذكر مسبوقة بالرقم - وإن كانت قد ذكرت أحاديث -، وإنما ذكر ص ٣٧٠ (الدليل الحادي عشر).
والثاني: أن هذه النسخة متصرف فيها.
٦ - ص ٣٦٩ (فلا يقول مثل هذا القول إلا عن. . . [وأشار الجامع رحمه الله إلى أن هنا بياضا في الأصل] بين والكذب على الله عز وجل أعظم من الكذب على رسوله).
قلت: ويظهر أن العبارة (إلا عن علم بين) أو نحوها.
٧ - ص ٣٧٣ (وأما الملائكة فإن حالهم اليوم شبيهة بحالهم بعد ذلك، فإن ثوابهم متصل وليست الجنة مخلوقة، وتصديق. . .).
قلت: ويظهر أن العبارة (وليست الجنة مخلوقة لهم).
٨ - ص ٣٤٧ (إن إجلاسه على العرش منكراً) والصواب: (منكر)
٩ - ص ٣٨٧: (ولا يقال إنه لما لم يقرن بالإنكار دل على أنه حق، فإن قولهن {مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا ً} خطأ. وقولهن: {إِنْ هَذَا إِلاَّ مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ} خطأ أيضًا في غيبتهن عنه أنه بشر وإثباتهن أنه ملك، وإن لم يقرن بالإنكار، [دل على أنه حق، وأن قولهن: {مَا هَذَا بَشَرًا إِنْ هَذَا إِلاَّ مَلَكٌ كَرِيمٌ} خطأ في نفيهن عنه البشرية وإثباتهن له الملائكية، وإن لم يقرن بالإنكار] لغيبة عقولهن عند رؤيته، فلم يلمن في تلك الحال على ذلك).
قلت: والذي يظهر أن ما بين المعقوفتين مكرر، والله أعلم.
translated_text:
exalted is He:

“Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, and they do not believe.”

And He said:

“And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, eyes with which they do not see, and ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless.”

Dawābb (“living creatures”) is the plural of dābba (“a living creature”), which includes everything that moves in heaven or on earth: humans, jinn, angels, and animals. Thus, five verses in the Quran indicate the superiority of animals over many humans. Ibn al-Marzubān wrote a book entitled The Superiority of Dogs over Many Who Wear Clothes. The transmitted reports on this subject are too numerous for us to count, including the following in Musnad Ahmad:

“Many a mount remembers Allah more than its rider.”

Animals are superior to such people in several respects:

First, an animal has no means of attaining greater perfection or soundness than it already displays, whereas a human being does. If a person fails to attain the soundness and perfection for which he was created, his deficiency and loss become apparent in this respect.

Second, animals have inclinations and desires corresponding to their sensations and awareness, but they have not been endowed with the ability to distinguish and discriminate between what benefits them and what harms them. Human beings, however, have been endowed with this ability.

This is the meaning of the saying: Angels have reason without desires; animals have desires without reason; and human beings have both desires and reason. Whoever’s reason prevails over his desires is superior to the angels, or like them; but whoever’s desires prevail over his reason is inferior to animals.

Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd said (pp. 38–43):

I wish to draw attention to two matters.

The first matter: I doubt that this treatise can be attributed to Shaykh al-Islām, may Allah have mercy on him. Anyone who has read the Shaykh’s writings and is familiar with his characteristic style in his treatises and fatwas will recognize this readily. Either the treatise originally belonged to the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, but his words were mixed with those of someone else without distinguishing between them, or it belongs to one of his students influenced by him, or something similar. That the entire treatise is his, however, strikes me as unlikely. Allah knows best. In general, the manner in which this treatise is written differs from the Shaykh’s style. I shall give some examples:

1 - P. 359: “This is the most astonishing marvel.”
2 - P. 364: “Understand this, for beneath it lies a secret.”
3 - Pp. 365–366: “Understand this, for it clears away doubt and filters out confusion.”
4 - P. 366: “Allah is supremely great.”
5 - Pp. 374–375: “Do not enter the door of denial, rejection, withholding assent, and turning a blind eye, rejecting its outward meaning and finding its inward meaning astonishing, merely to preserve the rules you have formulated through your own faculties and regulated by principles that have kept you from the presence of your Lord. Beware of anything contrary to the predecessors’ affirmation of divine transcendence, and avoid likening or comparing Him to creation. By my life, this is indeed the straight path, sharper than a sword and finer than a hair. Whoever Allah does not grant light has no light.”
6 - P. 352: “I have no knowledge of its true nature”; p. 353: “This is unknown, and Allah knows His creation best”; p. 354: “But what occurred to me—and Allah knows best what is correct”; p. 361: “Perhaps that is so, and Allah knows the realities of things best”; p. 364: “We have no need to interpret our Lord’s words through our own opinions. Allah knows their interpretation best.”
7 - P. 374: “This is a sea in which even a swimmer drowns. None ventures into it except someone supported by the light of guidance; otherwise, he falls into either likening Allah to creation or denying His attributes. Let the discerning person recognize that beyond his knowledge lies a distant reach, and above everyone possessing knowledge is one more knowledgeable.”
8 - P. 375: “Even if it were established that human knowledge in this world comes only through the angels—which, by Allah, is false.”
9 - P. 379: “This, may Allah guide you, is the basis for superiority according to the known grounds, of which we have given an example”; p. 381: “Know—may Allah illuminate your heart and open your breast to Islam.”

Second: He describes his opponents in ways unfamiliar in his writings, such as:

1 - P. 358: “Some fools have said that the prostration was only to Allah, with Adam made their direction of prayer.”
2 - P. 362: “Know, first, that this assertion has nothing requiring its acceptance, whether transmitted evidence or rational argument—only passing thoughts, sudden notions, and insinuations whose substance comes from the throne of Iblīs.”
3 - P. 363: “Anyone in whose inner thoughts the possibility of restriction still stirs after this verification and tawkīl (entrusting) should offer himself condolences for his ability to reason from the Quran and understand it, for he cannot trust anything derived from it. If only I knew! If all the angels had prostrated and Allah wished to tell us this, what wording could be more complete and comprehensive? Or could any statement be made of which one would not say: ‘Is this not among the clearest expressions?’”
4 - P. 376: “It is not as this fool claims.”
5 - P. 391: “This is among the clearest statements for anyone who understands Arabic. We seek refuge in Allah from excessive pedantry.”

Third: On p. 379, while arguing for the superiority of righteous humans over angels, he says: “How do they compare with those who ‘give others preference over themselves, even though they are in need’? How do they compare with those who call to guidance and the religion of truth, or someone who establishes a good practice? How do they compare with those mentioned in his saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Among my community are those who will intercede for more people than Rabīʿa and Mudar’? How do they compare with the aqtāb, awtād, aghwāth, abdāl, and nujabāʾ?”

The compiler, may Allah have mercy on him, commented on the last sentence: “Thus in the original.” This indicates that he found such wording objectionable. The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, has statements refuting these designations and explaining that they occur in neither the Quran nor the sunnah. These include:

His statement in al-Fatāwā, 11:433: “As for the names circulating on the tongues of many ascetics and ordinary people, such as the ghawth in Mecca, the four awtād, the seven aqtāb, the forty abdāl, and the three hundred nujabāʾ: these names do not occur in the Book of Allah Most High, nor are they transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through either an authentic or a weak chain of transmission…” The fatwa continues at considerable length and in detail.

He also said in al-Minhāj, 1:93: “Furthermore, no one has transmitted through a known chain of transmission that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used any of these expressions—ghawth, qutb, awtād, nujabāʾ, and others—or that his Companions did. However, some of the predecessors used the term abdāl, and a weak hadith concerning it is related from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

In short, the style of this treatise is not the characteristic style of Shaykh al-Islām, may Allah have mercy on him, in his treatises. Allah knows best.

The second matter: A few textual corruptions have occurred in this treatise, including:

1 - P. 353: “Within the inferior category there may be something better than many individual members of the superior category, as with a donkey, a mouse, and a disabled horse, and a righteous woman alongside a wicked man.”

I say: Kāl-himār wa-l-faʾra (“as with a donkey and a mouse”) should read kāl-himār al-fārih (“as with a vigorous donkey”).

2 - P. 357: “ʿAbd Allāh related it in al-Tafsīr.” He previously mentioned this report on p. 244, saying: “ʿAbd Allāh in al-Sunan.” On p. 369, the title appears as al-Sunnah, which seems more likely. Allah knows best.

3 - P. 360: “Animals do not worship Allah.” Perhaps it should read: “They worship none but Allah.”

4 - P. 364: “If the account has been repeated and contains nothing indicating restriction, then claiming restriction in it is not a false allegation.”

I say: The wording appears to be: “Claiming restriction in it was a false allegation,” or: “Then claiming restriction…,” or something similar.

5 - P. 368: He mentions the eighth proof, then says in the twelfth line: “Then he mentioned what al-Khallāl related…” This indicates two things:

First, that abridgment has taken place, because the “ninth proof” and the “tenth” were not introduced with their numbers, although hadiths were mentioned. Only on p. 370 does he mention the “eleventh proof.”

Second, that this copy has been altered.

6 - P. 369: “Such a statement can only be made on the basis of … [the compiler, may Allah have mercy on him, indicated that there is a blank here in the original] that is clear. Lying about Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is more serious than lying about His Messenger.”

I say: The wording appears to be: “Only on the basis of clear knowledge,” or something similar.

7 - P. 373: “As for the angels, their condition today resembles their condition thereafter, for their reward is continuous, and Paradise is not created, and affirmation…”

I say: The wording appears to be: “And Paradise is not created for them.”

8 - P. 347: “Indeed, seating him upon the Throne is objectionable”—munkaran. The correct form is munkar.

9 - P. 387: “It should not be said that, because it was not accompanied by a denunciation, this indicated that it was true. Their statement, ‘This is not a human being,’ was mistaken, and their statement, ‘This is nothing but a noble angel,’ was also mistaken, in their failure to recognize that he was human and their assertion that he was an angel, even though it was not accompanied by a denunciation, [indicated that it was true, and their statement, ‘This is not a human being; this is nothing but a noble angel,’ was mistaken in their denial of his humanity and their assertion that he was an angel, even though it was not accompanied by a denunciation] because they lost their senses upon seeing him. They were therefore not blamed for this in that state.”

I say: What appears within square brackets seems to be a repetition. Allah knows best.

Third, these people face punishment, exemplary chastisement, and disgrace for the wicked deeds they commit: one is executed, another punished, another subjected to amputation, and another made to suffer and imprisoned. These are punishments prescribed by religious law. As for decreed punishments, some peoples were drowned, others destroyed by various forms of torment, and others afflicted with unjust rulers who subjected them to burning, drowning, mutilation, strangulation, and blinding. Animals are safe from all this.

Fourth, the wicked among the jinn and mankind will face horrors, the Fire, torment, shackles, and other things in the Hereafter from which animals are safe. Comparing their respective conditions makes clear the superiority of animals over these people.

Fifth, all animals believe in Allah and His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; they glorify Allah with praise and are obedient to Him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“There is nothing on the face of the earth that does not know that I am the Messenger of Allah, except the wicked among the jinn and mankind.”

The second form of comparison is to say that humanity as a whole is superior to the angels as a whole, without comparing individuals. On the view that righteous human beings are superior to the angels, this claim remains open to question; I do not know whether it is true. For we regard the second generation as a whole as superior to the third generation, although we know that many people of the third generation are superior to many people of the second.

The third form of comparison is this: if we compare the superior members of each kind, then those next in rank with their counterparts in the other kind, which of the two groups is superior?

On the view that righteous human beings are superior, one may say: there is no doubt that the lower-ranking angels are superior to many human beings, while the superior human beings are superior to the superior angels. The fourth form is to ask: is the essence of an angel and angelic nature superior, or the essence of a human being and human nature?

This is comparable to our knowing that a living being, insofar as it is alive, is superior to a dead one; that strength and knowledge, considered as such, are superior to weakness and ignorance; that the male essence is superior to the female essence; and that the essence of a horse is superior to that of a donkey.  أَنَّا إذَا اعْتَبَرْنَا الْحَقِيقَتَيْنِ وَصِفَاتِهِمَا النَّفْسِيَّةَ وَالتَّبَعِيَّةَ: اللَّازِمَةُ الْغَالِبَةُ الْحَيَاةُ وَالْعِلْمُ وَالْقُدْرَةُ: فِي اللَّذَّاتِ وَالشَّهَوَاتِ وَجَدْنَا أَوَّلًا خَلْقَ الْمَلَكِ أَعْظَمُ صُورَةً وَمَحَلَّهُ أَرْفَعَ وَحَيَاتَهُ أَشَدَّ وَعِلْمَهُ أَكْثَرَ وَقُوَاهُ أَشَدَّ وَطَهَارَتَهُ وَنَزَاهَتَهُ أَتَمَّ وَنَيْلَ مَطَالِبِهِ أَيْسَرَ وَأَتَمَّ وَهُوَ عَنْ الْمُنَافِي وَالْمُضَادِّ أَبْعَدُ لَكِنْ تَجِدُ هَذِهِ الصِّفَاتِ لِلْإِنْسَانِ - بِحَسَبِ حَقِيقَتِهِ - مِنْهَا أَوْفَرَ حَظًّا وَنَصِيبًا مِنْ الْحَيَاةِ وَالْخَلْقِ وَالْعِلْمِ وَالْقُدْرَةِ وَالطَّهَارَةِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ.
 وَلَهُ أَشْيَاءُ لَيْسَتْ لِلْمَلَكِ مِنْ إدْرَاكِهِ دَقِيقَ الْأَشْيَاءِ:
 حِسًّا وَعَقْلًا وَتَمَتُّعُهُ بِمَا يُدْرِكُهُ بِبَدَنِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَهُوَ يَأْكُلُ وَيَشْرَبُ وَيَنْكِحُ وَيَتَمَنَّى وَيَتَغَذَّى
translated_text:
and an angel: you may mean this particular human being, in which case the reference is particular; or the entire human species, in which case it is general; or the human being without qualification, abstracted from any restriction to the general or particular, its numerical scope being expressed as few or many. The first form concerns superiority both generally and particularly; the second, generally; the third, particularly; and the fourth concerns essence considered without qualification and in abstraction.

We may then say:

As regards the question considered in this way, I know of no earlier statement that explains it. Some people may have argued for the superiority of angels, and others for the superiority of human beings. This question may also have been confused with that of superiority between the righteous and others. Yet what has occurred to me—and Allah knows best what is correct—is that angelic essence is more perfect and more exalted, while human essence is simpler and more comprehensive.

The explanation is as follows:

When we consider the two essences and their intrinsic and consequent attributes, whether inseparable or predominant—life, knowledge, and power in relation to pleasures and desires—we find, first, that the angel is created with a grander form; his abode is higher; his life is more vigorous; his knowledge is greater; his faculties are stronger; his purity and freedom from defilement are more complete; and his attainment of what he seeks is easier and more complete. He is also further removed from whatever is incompatible with him or opposed to him. Yet these attributes are also found in the human being, according to his essence, with a more abundant share of them—of life, physical constitution, knowledge, power, purity, and so forth.

The human being also possesses things that the angel does not: his perception of subtle things through the senses and the intellect, and his enjoyment, in body and heart, of what he perceives. He eats, drinks, has sexual relations, forms wishes, and takes nourishment

{مِمَّنْ}

 فَإِنْ قُلْت:
 هَذَا الِاسْتِدْلَالُ مَفْهُومٌ لِلْمُخَالِفِ وَأَنْتَ مُخَالِفٌ لِهَذَا مُنَازِعٌ فِيهِ.
translated_text:
and reflects, among other activities in which the angel does not share. Yet the angel has a greater share of what they have in common, and the qualities they share are far superior to those peculiar to the human being.

“An illustration”: one man has a hundred dinars, while another has fifty dirhams, or fifty dinars, or fifty copper coins. Since this is so, the decisive answer is as stated above.

If, however, you seek an unqualified judgment, angelic essence, together with its necessary attributes, is superior to human essence with its necessary attributes. There is no doubt about this. For the life, sensory perception, knowledge, action, attainment of pleasure, and fulfillment of desire necessarily belonging to human essence are of little account. Its forms are merely more numerous in comparison with what resembles angelic essence. It is like comparing someone who knows a little about everything with someone who has mastered knowledge of Allah, His names, and His signs. The condition of someone possessing a dirham is not comparable to that of someone possessing a pearl, nor is the condition of someone who governs all people comparable to that of someone who governs one human being and a horse.

This is clearly indicated by the words of the Most High:

“We have certainly honored the children of Adam, carried them on land and sea, provided them with good things, and favored them greatly above many of those We have created.”

This indicates that they have not been favored above all. His word “mimman” (“of those”) is partitive.

If you say: “This argument rests on an implication drawn by the opposing party, yet you oppose and dispute it.”

فَيُقَالُ لَك:
 تَخْصِيصُ الْكَثِيرِ بِالذِّكْرِ لَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى مُخَالَفَةِ غَيْرِهِ بِنَفْيٍ وَلَا إثْبَاتٍ وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ مَفْهُومَهُ: أَنَّهُمْ لَمْ يُفَضِّلُوا عَلَى مَا سِوَى الْكَثِيرِ فَإِذَا لَمْ يُفَضِّلُوا فَقَدْ يُسَاوُونَ بِهِمْ وَقَدْ يُفَضِّلُ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَإِنَّ الْأَحْوَالَ ثَلَاثَةٌ: إمَّا أَنْ يُفَضِّلُوا عَلَى مَنْ بَقِيَ أَوْ يُفَضِّلُ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَوْ يُسَاوُونَ بِهِمْ.

وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ جَمَاعَةٌ مِنْ الْمُنْتَسِبِينَ إلَى السُّنَّةِ:

 وَذَكَرَ لِي عَنْ بَعْضِ مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ فِي أَعْمَالِ الْقُلُوبِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 أَمَّا الْمَلَائِكَةُ الْمُدَبِّرُونَ لِلسَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَالْمُوَكَّلُونَ بِبَنِي آدَمَ؛ فَهَؤُلَاءِ أَفْضَلُ
translated_text:
The reply to you is:

Singling out the many for mention does not imply a different judgment concerning the rest, whether affirmative or negative. Moreover, its implication is that they have not been favored above those outside the many. If they have not been favored above them, they may be equal to them, or those others may be superior to them. There are three possibilities: either they are superior to those who remain, those others are superior to them, or they are equal to them.

He said:

Differences in essential natures and essences necessarily affect the judgments and attributes pertaining to them. If the essential natures of humans and angels differ, one of the two must be superior, for it is impossible for them to be both identical and unequal in excellence. Once this rational proposition establishes that one is superior, and that divine statement establishes that humans are not superior, the superiority of angels is established—which is the point to be proved.

Several of those who affiliate themselves with the Sunnah have stated that the prophets and righteous human beings are superior to the angels. The Mu‘tazilah hold that angels are superior to humans, while the followers of al-Ash‘arī hold two positions: some consider the prophets and Allah’s friends superior, while others suspend judgment and make no categorical assertion as to which of the two is superior. It has been reported that some of their later scholars inclined toward the position of the Mu‘tazilah. This view has also sometimes been attributed to some who profess adherence to the Sunnah and support it.

It was related to me that someone who discussed deeds of the heart said:

“As for the angels who govern the heavens, the earth, and what lies between them, and those entrusted with the children of Adam, these are superior

As for the karūbiyyūn (cherubim), who stand above such tasks, no one is superior to them.” Some of them may make an exception for our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. His exclusion from the general judgment concerning humanity means deeming him superior either to every individual angel or to those angels who govern the affairs of the world.

This is what has reached me of others’ statements on this question. I had thought that discussion of it was a later development, until I discovered that it was grounded in transmitted reports, going back to the early generations and the Companions. This prompted me to investigate the matter thoroughly, whereupon we adopted the position of the early generations.

Abū Ya‘lā al-Mawsilī related in his well-known Kitāb al-Tafsīr (Book of Quranic Commentary) a report from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Salām. He was knowledgeable about both the earlier and the later Scripture, having been one of the People of the Book. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had testified that his life would end well; Mu‘ādh’s counsel at his death also identified him as one of the four scholars from whom knowledge should be sought. He said:

“Allah has created no creature more honored by Him than Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” This is the report related from him.

I asked, “Not even Gabriel or Michael?”

He replied, “My nephew, do you know what Gabriel and Michael are? Gabriel and Michael are merely creatures subjected to Allah’s command, like the sun and the moon. Allah Most High has created no creature more honored by Him than Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

‘Abd Allāh also related in al-Tafsīr (Quranic Commentary) (*) and elsewhere, from Ma‘mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that he said:

“The angels said, ‘Our Lord, You have given the children of Adam this world, where they eat and drink; so grant us the Hereafter.’

“He replied, ‘By My might, I will not make the righteous among the descendants of the one whom I created with My two hands like those to whom I said, “Be,” and they came into being.’”
translated_footnote: (*) Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd (p. 256) said: “Perhaps this should read al-Sunna.”

Likewise, there is the account of the angels, all of them without exception, prostrating to Adam, and of the curse upon the one who refused to prostrate to him. This bestowed honor and dignity upon Adam.

Some foolish people have said: “The prostration was only to Allah, and Adam was made their direction of prayer, so that they prostrated toward him just as one prostrates toward the Ka‘bah. This does not establish his superiority over them, just as prostrating toward the Ka‘bah does not establish its superiority over a believer in Allah’s sight. Indeed, a believer’s sanctity is greater in Allah’s sight than that of the Ka‘bah.” They also said: “Prostrating to anyone other than Allah is forbidden; indeed, it is disbelief.”

The answer is that the prostration was to Adam, by Allah’s command and as an obligation He imposed, according to the consensus of all whose opinions carry weight. Several points demonstrate this:

First, He said “to Adam,” not “toward Adam.” Each preposition has its own meaning, and the language distinguishes between saying “I prostrated to him” and “I prostrated toward him.” As Allah Most High says:

“Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.”

And He says:

“To Allah prostrate all those in the heavens and the earth.”

Muslims unanimously agree that prostrating to anyone other than Allah is forbidden. As for the Ka‘bah, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray toward Jerusalem, then prayed toward the Ka‘bah. He would pray toward a short spear—not ‘to a short spear’—and toward a tree trunk—not ‘to a trunk’ or ‘to a tree.’ One who prostrates to something submits and humbles himself before it in his heart. By contrast, one who prostrates toward something merely turns his face and body toward it outwardly, just as he turns his face toward some

“So turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.”

Second, if Adam had merely been a direction of prayer, Iblīs would not have refused to prostrate or claimed that he was better than Adam. A direction of prayer may consist of stones, without this making them superior to those who pray toward them. A man may pray toward a short spear, a camel, or another man, without imagining that this makes any of them superior. What, then, was Satan trying to avoid? This is truly astonishing!

Third, if He had made Adam the direction of prayer for a single prostration, then the direction of prayer and Jerusalem would have been many thousands of times superior to him, since they were made permanent directions for every kind of prayer. Thus, this lengthy account—which has been made a mark of his distinction and one of the greatest blessings bestowed upon him, and which has conveyed to the world that Allah elevated him through it and favored him—would amount to no more than His making him like the Ka‘bah on certain occasions. Yet even some of the faith, knowledge, and closeness to the Most Merciful that he was granted are far superior to the Ka‘bah; indeed, the Ka‘bah was established for him and his descendants. Is this, then, to be counted among the great blessings bestowed upon him, or is he to be likened to it in some exceedingly small and insignificant respect? No rational person would say this.

As for their statement, “It is not permissible to prostrate to anyone other than Allah,” the answer is: if this is stated in general terms, it is a general statement whose scope excludes the permissibility of prostrating to Adam. Yet specific evidence establishes that they prostrated to him, and a general statement does not override the specific evidence that qualifies it.

Second, they claim that prostrating to anyone other than Allah is forbidden both to us and to the angels. As for the former, there is no evidence; as for the latter, what proof is there for it?

translated_text:
Third, do they mean that it is forbidden even when Allah commands it, or that it is forbidden when He has not commanded it? The latter is true, but it does not resolve the issue. As for the former, how could it be forbidden after Allah the Exalted has commanded it?

Fourth, Joseph’s father and brothers fell down in prostration to him, and it is said that this was their form of greeting. How, then, can prostration be said to be forbidden without qualification? Animals also used to prostrate to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, yet animals do not worship Allah. How, then, can it be said that prostrating to something necessarily entails worshipping it? The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“If I were to command anyone to prostrate to anyone else, I would command a wife to prostrate to her husband.”

This is because of the greatness of his right over her. It is well known that he did not say, “If I were to command anyone to worship.”

Seventh (1), the explanation here is as follows: submission and heartfelt devotion, together with acknowledgment of lordship and servitude, can, in an absolute sense, be directed only to Allah—glorified and exalted be He—alone. Directing them to anyone else is impossible and invalid. Prostration, however, is one of the ordinances of revealed law, for Allah the Exalted has commanded us to prostrate to Him. Had He commanded us to prostrate to any of His creatures other than Himself, we would have prostrated to that creature in obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since He would have wished us to honor the one to whom we prostrated. Had He not made prostration obligatory for us, performing it would not have been obligatory at all.

Thus, the angels’ prostration to Adam was worship of Allah, obedience to Him, and an act through which they drew near to Him; for Adam, it conferred distinction, honor, and reverence. Joseph’s brothers’ prostration to him was a greeting and salutation. Do you not see that, had Joseph prostrated to his parents as a greeting, this would not have been deemed reprehensible for him?

وَلَمْ يَأْتِ أَنَّ آدَمَ سَجَدَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ بَلْ لَمْ يُؤْمَرْ آدَمَ وَبَنُوهُ بِالسُّجُودِ إلَّا لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَلَعَلَّ ذَلِكَ - وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِحَقَائِقِ الْأُمُورِ - لِأَنَّهُمْ أَشْرَفُ الْأَنْوَاعِ وَهُمْ صَالِحُو بَنِي آدَمَ لَيْسَ فَوْقَهُمْ أَحَدٌ يُحْسِنُ السُّجُودُ لَهُ إلَّا لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَهُمْ أَكْفَاءٌ بَعْضُهُمْ لِبَعْضِ فَلَيْسَ لِبَعْضِهِمْ مَزِيَّةٌ بِقَدْرِ مَا يَصْلُحُ لَهُ السُّجُودُ وَمَنْ سِوَاهُمْ فَقَدْ سَجَدَ لَهُمْ مِنْ الْمَلَائِكَةِ لِلْأَبِ الْأَقْوَمُ وَمِنْ الْبَهَائِمِ لِلِابْنِ الْأَكْرَمُ.
 وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُمْ:
 لَمْ يَسْبِقْ لِآدَمَ مَا يُوجِبُ الْإِكْرَامَ لَهُ بِالسُّجُودِ فَلَغْوٌ مِنْ الْقَوْلِ هذي بِهِ بَعْضُ مَنْ اعْتَزَلَ الْجَمَاعَةَ فَإِنَّ نَعَمْ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَأَيَادِيهِ وَآلَائِهِ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ لَيْسَتْ بِسَبَبِ مِنْهُمْ وَلَوْ كَانَتْ بِسَبَبِ مِنْهُمْ فَهُوَ الْمُنْعِمُ بِذَلِكَ السَّبَبِ فَهُوَ الْمُنْعِمُ بِهِ وَيَشْكُرُهُمْ عَلَى نِعَمِهِ؛ وَهُوَ أَيْضًا بَاطِلٌ عَلَى قَاعِدَتِهِمْ لَا حَاجَةَ لَنَا إلَى بَيَانِهِ هَاهُنَا.
 وَقَوْلُهُ:
 
{وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ}
 فَإِنَّهُ إنْ سُلِّمَ أَنَّهُ يُفِيدُ الْحَصْرَ فَالْقَصْدُ مِنْهُ - وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ -
 الْفَضْلُ بَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ الْبَشَرِ الَّذِينَ يُشْرِكُونَ بِرَبِّهِمْ وَيَعْبُدُونَ غَيْرَهُ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ أَنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ لَا تَعْبُدُ غَيْرَهُ ثُمَّ هَذَا عَامٌّ وَتِلْكَ الْآيَةُ خَاصَّةٌ فَيُسْتَثْنَى آدَمَ ثُمَّ يُقَالُ:
 السُّجُودُ عَلَى ضَرْبَيْنِ سُجُودُ عِبَادَةٍ مَحْضَةٍ وَسُجُودُ تَشْرِيفٍ. فَأَمَّا الْأَوَّلُ فَلَا يَكُونُ إلَّا لِلَّهِ وَأَمَّا الثَّانِي فَلِمَ قُلْت إنَّهُ كَذَلِكَ؟ وَالْآيَةُ مَحْمُولَةٌ عَلَى الْأَوَّلِ تَوْفِيقًا بَيْنَ الدَّلَائِلِ.
 وَأَمَّا السُّؤَالُ الثَّانِي فَرُوِيَ عَنْ بَعْضِ الْأَوَّلِينَ:
 أَنَّ الْمَلَائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ
translated_text:
Nor has it been reported that Adam prostrated to the angels. Rather, Adam and his descendants were commanded to prostrate only to Allah, Lord of all worlds. Perhaps this—and Allah knows best the realities of all things—is because they are the noblest kind of beings, namely, the righteous descendants of Adam. There is no one above them to whom prostration would be fitting except Allah, Lord of all worlds. They are equals among themselves, and none possesses such an advantage over the others as would warrant prostration to him. As for other beings, they have prostrated to them: the angels to the most upright father, and the animals to the noblest son.

As for their claim, “Adam had done nothing beforehand to warrant being honored with prostration,” this is empty talk babbled by some of those who withdrew from the community. Allah the Exalted’s blessings, favors, and bounties upon His servants are not bestowed because of anything on their part. Even if they were bestowed because of something on their part, He Himself would be the One who had bestowed that very cause. Thus, He bestows it upon them and then shows them appreciation for His own blessings. Their claim is also invalid according to their own principles, though we need not explain that here.

As for His saying:

“And to Him they prostrate,”

even if it is conceded that this conveys exclusivity, its purpose—and Allah knows best—is to show their superiority to those human beings who associate partners with their Lord and worship others besides Him. He therefore informs them that the angels worship none besides Him. Moreover, this statement is general, whereas that verse is specific, so Adam is excepted. It may then be said: prostration is of two kinds—prostration purely as worship, and prostration to confer honor. The first can be directed only to Allah. As for the second, why do you say that the same applies to it? The verse is understood as referring to the first kind, thereby reconciling the evidence.

سَجَدُوا لِآدَمَ مَلَائِكَةٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَقَطْ؛ لَا مَلَائِكَةُ السَّمَوَاتِ.
 وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 مَلَائِكَةُ السَّمَوَاتِ دُونَ الكروبيين وَانْتَحَى ذَلِكَ بَعْضُ الْمُتَأَخِّرِينَ وَاسْتَنْكَرَ سُجُودَ الْأَعْلَيَيْنِ مِنْ الْمَلَائِكَةِ لِآدَمَ مَعَ عَدَمِ الْتِفَاتِهِمْ إلَى مَا سِوَى اللَّهِ وَرَوَوْا فِي ذَلِكَ: 
" إنَّ مِنْ خَلْقِ اللَّهِ خَلْقٌ لَا يَدْرُونَ: أَخُلِقَ آدَمَ أَمْ لَا "
؟
 وَنَزَعَ بِقَوْلِهِ:
 
{أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعَالِينَ}
 وَالْعَالُونَ هُمْ مَلَائِكَةُ السَّمَاءِ وَمَلَائِكَةُ السَّمَاءِ لَمْ يُؤْمَرُوا بِالسُّجُودِ لِآدَمَ فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْمَقَالَةَ أَوَّلًا لَيْسَ مَعَهَا مَا يُوجِبُ قَبُولَهَا؛ لَا مَسْمُوعٌ وَلَا مَعْقُولٌ إلَّا خَوَاطِرُ وَسَوَانِحُ وَوَسَاوِسُ مَادَّتُهَا مِنْ عَرْشِ إبْلِيسَ يَسْتَفِزُّهُمْ بِصَوْتِهِ لِيَرُدَّ عَنْهُمْ النِّعْمَةَ الَّتِي حَرَصَ عَلَى رَدِّهَا عَنْ أَبِيهِمْ قَدِيمًا أَوْ مَقَالَةٌ قَدْ قَالَهَا مَنْ يَقُولُ الْحَقَّ وَالْبَاطِلَ لَكِنَّ مَعَنَا مَا يُوجِبُ رَدَّهَا مِنْ وُجُوهٍ.
 أَحَدُهَا:
 أَنَّهُ خِلَافَ مَا عَلَيْهِ الْعَامَّةُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ بِالْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ وَإِذَا كَانَ لَا بُدَّ مِنْ التَّقْلِيدِ فَتَقْلِيدُهُمْ أَوْلَى.
 وَثَانِيهَا:
 أَنَّهُ خِلَافُ ظَاهِرِ الْكِتَابِ الْعَزِيزِ وَخِلَافُ نَصِّهِ فَإِنَّ الِاسْمَ الْمَجْمُوعَ الْمُعَرَّفَ بِالْأَلِفِ وَاللَّامِ يُوجِبُ اسْتِيعَابَ الْجِنْسِ قَالَ تَعَالَى: 
{وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ}
 فَسُجُودُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ يَقْتَضِي جَمِيعَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ هَذَا مُقْتَضَى اللِّسَانِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ بِهِ الْقُرْآنُ فَالْعُدُولُ عَنْ مُوجِبِ الْقَوْلِ الْعَامِّ إلَى الْخُصُوصِ لَا بُدَّ لَهُ مِنْ دَلِيلٍ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ وَهُوَ مَعْدُومٌ.
translated_text:
prostrated to Adam were only angels on earth, not the angels of the heavens.

Others say they were the angels of the heavens, excluding the cherubim. A later writer adopted this view and found it inconceivable that the most exalted angels should prostrate to Adam, given that they pay no heed to anything other than Allah. They related in support of this:

“Among Allah’s creatures are beings who do not know whether Adam was created or not.”

He also appealed to Allah’s words:

“Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted?”

He took “the exalted” to mean the angels of heaven, maintaining that the angels of heaven were not commanded to prostrate to Adam.

Know, then, that this claim has, in the first place, no support warranting its acceptance, whether from transmitted evidence or rational argument. It rests on nothing but passing thoughts, fleeting notions, and insinuations whose source is the throne of Iblīs. He incites them with his voice to deprive them of the blessing he strove to withhold from their father long ago. Or else it is a statement made by someone who speaks both truth and falsehood. We, however, have grounds for rejecting it on several counts.

First, it contradicts the position held by the general body of scholars versed in the Book and the Sunnah. If one must follow others on their authority, these scholars are more deserving of being followed.

Second, it contradicts both the apparent meaning of the Noble Book and its explicit wording. A plural noun made definite by the definite article encompasses the entire class it denotes. Allah the Exalted says:

“And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam.’”

Thus, the angels’ prostration includes all the angels. This is what the language in which the Quran was revealed entails. Departing from the scope of a general statement by restricting it to particular members requires adequate evidence, and no such evidence exists.

original_text:
وَثَالِثُهَا:
 أَنَّهُ قَالَ: 
{فَسَجَدَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ}
 فَلَوْ لَمْ يَكُنْ الِاسْمُ الْأَوَّلُ يَقْتَضِي الِاسْتِيعَابَ وَالِاسْتِغْرَاقَ لَكَانَ تَوْكِيدُهُ بِصِيغَةِ كُلٍّ مُوجِبَةً لِذَلِكَ وَمُقْتَضِيَةً لَهُ ثُمَّ لَوْ لَمْ يُفِدْ تِلْكَ الْإِفَادَةَ لَكَانَ قَوْلُهُ أَجْمَعُونَ تَوْكِيدًا وَتَحْقِيقًا بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدٍ وَتَحْقِيقٍ وَمَنْ نَازَعَ فِي مُوجِبِ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْعَامَّةِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُنَازِعُ فِيهَا بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا بِمَا يُفِيدُ الْعُمُومَ بَلْ إنَّمَا يُجَاءُ بِصِيغَةِ التَّوْكِيدِ قَطْعًا لِاحْتِمَالِ الْخُصُوصِ وَأَشْبَاهِهِ.
 وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِي عَنْ بَعْضِ السَّلَف أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 مَا ابْتَدَعَ قَوْمٌ بِدْعَةً إلَّا فِي الْقُرْآنِ مَا يَرُدُّهَا وَلَكِنْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ فَلَعَلَّ قَوْلَهُ: 
{كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ}
 جِيءَ بِهِ لِزَعْمِ زَاعِمٍ يَقُولُ: إنَّمَا سَجَدَ لَهُ بَعْضُ الْمَلَائِكَةِ لَا كُلُّهُمْ وَكَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ رَدًّا لِمَقَالَةِ هَؤُلَاءِ.
 وَمَنْ اخْتَلَجَ فِي سِرِّهِ وَجْهَ الْخُصُوصِ بَعْدَ هَذَا التَّحْقِيقِ وَالتَّوْكِيدِ فَلْيَعُزْ نَفْسَهُ فِي الِاسْتِدْلَالِ بِالْقُرْآنِ وَالْفَهْمِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَثِقُ بِشَيْءِ يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهُ يَا لَيْتَ شِعْرِي لَوْ كَانَتْ الْمَلَائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ سَجَدُوا وَأَرَادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُخْبِرَنَا بِذَلِكَ فَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ أَتَمُّ وَأَعَمُّ أَمْ يَأْتِي قَوْلٌ يُقَالُ:
 أَلَيْسَ هَذَا مِنْ أَبْيَنِ الْبَيَانِ؟ .
وَرَابِعُهَا:
 أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةَ تَكَرَّرَتْ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي حَدِيثِ الشَّفَاعَةِ 
{وَأَسْجَدَ لَك مَلَائِكَتَهُ}
 وَكَذَلِكَ فِي مُحَاجَّةِ مُوسَى وَآدَمَ وَمِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إنَّ الْقَوْلَ الْعَامَّ إذَا قُرِنَ بِهِ الْخَاصُّ وَجَبَ أَنْ يُقْرَنَ بِهِ الْبَيَانُ فَلَا يَجُوزُ تَأْخِيرُهُ عَنْهُ لِئَلَّا يَقَعَ السَّامِعُ فِي اعْتِقَادِ الْجَهْلِ؛ وَلَمْ يَقْتَرِنْ بِشَيْءِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَاتِ دَلِيلُ تَخْصِيصٍ فَوَجَبَ الْقَطْعُ بِالْعُمُومِ. وَقَالَ آخَرُونَ - وَهُوَ الْأَصْوَبُ -: يَجُوزُ تَأْخِيرُ الْبَيَانِ عَنْ وَقْتِ الْخِطَابِ
translated_text:
Third, He says:

“So the angels prostrated, all of them without exception.”

Even if the noun “angels” did not itself encompass every member of the class, reinforcing it with “all” would necessarily convey that meaning. Even if this did not suffice, “without exception” would provide yet further emphasis and confirmation. Even those who dispute the implications of general terms do not dispute them once they are reinforced by expressions conveying universality. Indeed, such emphatic expressions are introduced precisely to exclude the possibility of restriction and similar interpretations.

It has reached me that one of the early generations said:

“No people introduce an innovation without there being something in the Quran that refutes it, though they do not know it.”

Perhaps His words, “all of them without exception,” were included to answer anyone who might claim that only some of the angels prostrated to him, not all of them. This expression would thus refute their claim.

Anyone who still inwardly entertains a restricted interpretation after such confirmation and emphasis should offer himself condolences over his understanding and his ability to draw evidence from the Quran, for he can have no confidence in anything derived from it. I wonder: if all the angels had prostrated and Allah wished to inform us of that, what wording could be more complete and comprehensive? What other statement could be made? Is this not among the clearest possible expressions?

Fourth, this expression occurs repeatedly in the Quran. In the hadith of intercession, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“And He made His angels prostrate to you.”

The same occurs in the account of the debate between Moses and Adam. Some maintain that when a general statement is accompanied by something specific, its clarification must accompany it and may not be delayed, lest the listener be led into an erroneous belief. None of these statements is accompanied by evidence restricting its scope, so their universality must be affirmed with certainty. Others maintain—and this is the more correct view—that clarification may be delayed beyond the time the statement is made

لَكِنْ بَعْدَ الْبَحْثِ عَنْ دَلِيلِ التَّخْصِيصِ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. فَيَجِبُ الْقَوْلُ بِالْعُمُومِ وَإِذَا كَانَتْ الْقِصَّةُ قَدْ تَكَرَّرَتْ وَلَيْسَ فِيهَا مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْخُصُوصِ فَلَيْسَ دَعْوَى الْخُصُوصِ فِيهَا مِنْ الْبُهْتَانِ. وَأَمَّا إنْكَارُهُمْ لِسُجُودِ الكروبيين فَلَيْسَ بِشَيْءِ لِأَنَّهُمْ سَجَدُوا طَاعَةً وَعِبَادَةً لِرَبِّهِمْ وَزَادَ قَائِلُ ذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ آدَمَ إذَا ثَبَتَ أَنَّهُمْ لَمْ يَسْجُدُوا وَالْحِكَايَاتُ الْمُرْسَلَةُ لَا تُقِيمُ حَقًّا وَلَا تَهْدِمُ بَاطِلًا؛ وَتَفْسِيرُهُمْ 
{الْعَالِينَ}
 بالكروبيين قَوْلٌ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى بِلَا عِلْمٍ وَلَا يُعْرَفُ ذَلِكَ عَنْ إمَامٍ مُتَّبَعٍ.
